FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Two observations of improper cooling methods were made:         1) In the walk-in cooler, a full hotel pan of pot pie filling was observed having been cooled several days prior. The pie filling was approximately six inches deep.     Train staff to cool cooked TCS foods in shallow pans where the depth of food is not greater than two and a half inches.        2) In the front display cooler, numerous small containers packaged for sale were observed still cooling: Chili, carnitas, fried rice, beef stew, vegetable curry. Temperatures were between 90F and 110F. No cooling methods were in use, since warm foods were in covered containers, set in a display case for sale.    Train staff to always use proper cooling methods (like spreading food out in shallow containers in the walk-in cooler) to fully cool them before packaging them for sale. The display cooler may not be used for cooling foods; it is for holding cold foods cold.          Person in Charge was allowed to correct the violation and salvage the food items by promptly emptying all packages of TCS foods into shallow pans to cool in the walk in cooler. (  All items had been made that morning and packaged in the last hour. Based on discussion, the items would not have been in the temperature danger zone for more than 90 minutes at the point they were observed by Inspector.)

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: The small containers of   Chili, carnitas, fried rice, beef stew, and vegetable curry observed cooling without proper methods were all tightly covered.       Train staff not to cover foods until they are fully cooled.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Observed quarter pans of cooked beets and cabbage and potatoes held at room temperature by the grill line. Items were at 49F. Staff indicated the items are removed from the cooler and held out during the busy time of breakfast, then returned to the cooler when breakfast ends.     This is not allowed.     Cooked potatoes, cabbage and beets are TCS foods that can support bacterial growth (such as Bacillus cereus) when left in the temperature danger zone for more than four hours. The practice of taking out these containers, then returning them to the cooler puts them at risk of accumulated time in the temperature danger zone over repeated service periods.     Inspector discussed with staff that if they reduce the amount of foods to small working portions that will be used up within about 30 minutes and are not returned to the cooler, these small working portions may safely be kept by the grill for quick access. Train staff accordingly.     Anything beyond a small working portion must be maintained in mechanical refrigeration at 41F or below.          (For the specific items observed during inspection, they had been prepared that same day and were not above 50F, so person in charge was able to remove them to the walk-in cooler and leave them uncovered to rapidly re-cool.)

Discussed with operator, who stated that the chicken gravy was made the night before and placed into the cooler at 11pm last night. It had not been removed from the cooler since then according to the operator. Explained that food not cooled within time/temperature cooling parameters can grow bacteria that can cause foodborne illness. Operator elected to discard product into trash bin immediately. A batch of gumbo was beginning to cool from preparation at the same time, so inspector worked with operator to divide batch into 2 inch metal pans on a speed rack and place into the Walk In Cooler for a demonstration on how effective cooling in shallow pans can be. Ensure cooling is done within time temperature limits for hot and cold/ambient foods or discard food product. Will provide cooling fact sheets with emailed report.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Two large containers of chicken gravy were observed stored in the Walk In Cooler and were improperly cooled. Containers were large and deep, and covered tightly while cooling. Discussed cooling hot batches of soups in shallow pans with lids off, and using ice wands to speed cooling process. Discussed using pre-chilled ingredients for ambient temperature foods that are not cooked and keeping lids off until fully cooled. Retrain staff and ensure that methods are used to allow for fast cooling of foods to keep harmful bacterial growth in control.

FoodCodeText: Keep all intake and exhaust air ducts and filters clean.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Cooked TCS foods were cooling in deeply filled in plastic buckets at depths exceeding 18 inches. Reviewed proper shallow pan cooling method with the owner, manager, and cook. Ensure that food is not filled above 2 inches when utilizing the shallow pan cooling method and placed into a refrigeration unit soon after the cooking process is finished. 30-60 minute counter top venting is acceptable if food temperatures don't fall below 135 degrees F in that timeframe.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: Cooked TCS foods were cooling while in covered containers. Reviewed successful cooling methods with the manager. Ensure that cooling foods remain uncovered until fully cooled.

FoodCodeText: Before using Time as a Public Health Control for TCS food develop, follow and keep written procedures onsite.

Discussed proper use of time as a public health control and am supplying a template with this report. Ensure that written procedures are developed, trained on and proper time control methods are in place before using time as a public health control. Once a product is managed by time it needs to continue to be managed by time and discarded if not sold within 4 hours.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Numerous TCS foods were observed above 41F in the kitchen:    - in the top sections of mechanical prep coolers (such as mayo-based dressings)    - on ice in bus tubs (such as chimichurri sauce)     - kept out of temperature control altogether (such as herbed butter)      - kept out of temperature control as a large working portion (pooled eggs)            Inspectors assisted Person in Charge with making corrections onsite: Butter was discarded; pooled eggs for scrambling were left in cold bottom section of prep cooler to re-cool; items found on ice were relocated to mechanical refrigeration of discarded based on individual risk assessment; items observed warm in prep cooler top were allowed to remain in service for only the next two hours then be discarded.          TCS foods must be maintained under temperature control, in mechanical refrigeration. Temperatures of 41F must be maintained - even during busy times.     If necessary with a couple key ingredients, a small working portion (that would be used up within 20 minutes) could be taken out and set by the cookline - but it should be used that quickly and never returned to the cooler.          Holding foods on ice is not allowed. An additional mechanical prep cooler was previously added to the kitchen line for the explicit purpose of ending the practice of setting TCS foods in tubs on ice.     Discussed with Persons in Charge that this unsafe practice must be ended immediately, even if the menu needs to be restricted.

Train staff to spread out the food in shallow metal pans, not deeper than 2 1/2 inches, and leave uncovered or only loosely covered to cool in the walk-in. The sanitizer is in tablet form and can leave a powdery film on hands and surfaces that the tablets touch. The employee then began putting croutons on salads without changing gloves. Discussed with Operations Manager that gloves used for different tasks must be discarded, hands must be washed, and new pair of gloves must be put on, especially when changing tasks from chemicals to food. Emphasized that working with chemicals with gloves and then working with food with the same gloves can contaminate food with the chemical residue. Person In Charge decided to discard croutons. Discontinue this practice immediately and retrain employees to be aware of what tasks they are working on and what tasks they are changing to, and whether they should be changing gloves. Monitor employees and correct deviations from safe food handling practices.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution:  • Within the concentration specified in 21CFR.178.1010, and  • According to the manufacturer/'s directions
InspectorComments: Steramine quat tablets were being used as the sanitize step in the 3 basin sink set up in place of the hot water dish machine's sanitization step. Concentration for ready-to-use sink was measured at 0PPM. When asked, employee who mixed the sinks stated they use three tablets in the sink. Employee did not measure concentration. inspector and Operations Manager adjusted the sink until it reached 200PPM.  Steramine quat sanitizer bucket was set up at the time of inspection. One tablet was used for the bucket. When measured by the inspector with quat test kit, the concentration was measured below 150PPM per the test kit. Another tablet was added to bring the concentration to 200PPM.   Make sure sanitizers are used according to directions on the label so that they are effectively sanitizing food contact surfaces, equipment and utensils. Retrain employees to use test kits to ensure sanitizers are at effective concentrations.

FoodCodeText: Discontinue storing food preparation or dispensing utensils in a container of water that is not maintained at 135 degrees F (57 degrees C) and not cleaned when empty.
InspectorComments: Rice scoop that had already been used to scoop cooked rice was observed stored in a cup of room temperature water. Discussed with person-in-charge that scoops kept in water must be hot held at 135F or above at all times. Alternatively, scoop can be stored out of water and be washed, rinsed and sanitized every 4 hours. Discontinue current practice and retrain staff to follow a safe alternative.

FoodCodeText: Develop written procedures for the raw animal food noncontinuous cooking process and obtain prior approval from the regulatory authority before implementation.
InspectorComments: Facility was cooking chicken wings using a non-continuous cooking process to 114-120F, cooling them in the cooler and then reheating the foods to over 165F without written procedures. It was discussed with owner that if the process is to be continued, a written plan must be developed and kept on site. An alternative is to cook chicken fully to 165F or above and maintain hot at 135F or above until they are ordered. A template will be provided for owner to review in the email with the report. Choose one of the two approved options: either develop written procedures for current cooking process for chicken, or discontinue current cooking process and cook chicken to 165F or above initially, then hot hold at 135F or above until product is served.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Cooked potato greens were observed cooling on the counter at 76F. When asked when the potato greens started cooling, the cook explained that they cool the greens on the counter overnight. They do not move the greens to temperature control at all during the cooling process. Discussed with staff that when cooking food, it must be cooled within 6 hours total from 135F to 70F or below in 2 hours, and then the remaining 4 hours it must be cooled to 41F or below to be safe. If it is not cooled within these time and temperature frames, it can grow bacteria that can make people really sick. Operator opted to discard the product. Discussed new cooling methods for operator to safely cool foods and will provide guidance documents to cool foods in small containers in rapid time. Cool hot cooked foods rapidly within a 6 hour time frame to ensure safe food.

FoodCodeText: Sanitize food contact surfaces before using and after cleaning.
InspectorComments: Person in charge reports coffee pot and coffee equipment are washed in a sink located inside the cabinet under the coffee maker counter. No sanitizing step is in use. Approved sanitizers would be either chlorine (concentration between 50ppm - 100ppm) or quaternary ammonium (concentration specified by manufacturer, usually 200ppm - 400ppm). FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Cooked whole chicken was observed cooling for 30 minutes on a sheet pan in the Walk In Cooler. Measurements were taken at 30 minutes cooling at 127F and 1 hour cooling at 112F. Discussed with Person in Charge that these cooling methods were not effective and that they needed to utilize a new method for faster cooling that would cool from 135F to  70F or below in 2 hours. Person In Charge placed the whole chickens in the blast chiller to cool more rapidly. Retrain employees to cool cooked food within safe time/temperature parameters of 135F to 70F or below within 2 hours, then to 41F or below within the remaining time for a total of 6 hours.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Whole cooked rotisserie chickens were observed cooling in the Walk In Cooler. Cooling time/temperature was not going to be met utilizing these methods. Discussed with Person in Charge that the food needs to be separated into smaller portions to cool using this method. Person in charge used the blast chiller on site to cool the chickens in whole form. Utilize methods and equipment that will cool food rapidly.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Noodles cooked 1.5 hours earlier were measured at 77F at the time of inspection. FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: Shallow pans were observed tightly covered with plastic cling film while cooling from room temperature preparation. Some foods that were also hot and cooled to cold were observed with condensate on the film, indicating that the heat had no place to escape from the pan while cooling. Discussed pulling a corner of the cling film back while cooling to allow air to escape and food to cool faster and more effectively. Retrain employees to use more effective cooling methods.

FoodCodeText: The licensee must train employees to report when they have any of the following:  • Symptoms of an illness that can be transmitted through food  • Infectious diseases that can be transmitted through food, as diagnosed by a health practitioner  • Exposure to a suspected or confirmed disease outbreak
InspectorComments: There was no employee illness log used to track employee illness reports at the time of inspection. Will provide Employee Illness log in emailed report to Person In Charge. Chef was knowledgeable in illness requirements but another person is in charge of employees calling in sick for work. Keep employee illness log on site and fill out with each employee illness occurrence.

FoodCodeText: Keep non-food contact equipment surfaces clean.
InspectorComments: Fryer Freezer door handle was observed with significant grease accumulation at the time of inspection. Discussed with Person In Charge to have staff clean handle more frequently to prevent build up of grease. Maintain clean to sight and touch.

FoodCodeText: Use only chemical sanitizers on food-contact surfaces that meet Title 40, Code of Federal Regulations requirements: • Part 180, section 180.940 • Part 180, subpart E, section 180.2020
InspectorComments: Sink & Surface sanitizer from the 3 basin sink sanitizer dispenser was measured at 1.0 oz/gal at the time of inspection. This is not within the recommended use range and is too strong. Diluted sanitizer with CFPM at the time of inspection and instructed them that this is to be done for every bucket and sink used to clean food contact surfaces and wash dishes until sanitizer dispenser can be repaired and dispenses 0.27 - 0.55 oz/gal concentration per manufacturer's instructions. Have dispenser serviced by professional company. Retrain employees to monitor concentration of sanitizer dispenser to ensure that it is within safe and effective range. Maintain sanitizer dispenser according to manufacturer's instructions.

FoodCodeText: Clean all physical facilities (floors, walls, ceilings). Keep them clean.
InspectorComments: Observed caulking behind 3 basin sink in Meat Cutting area to be moldy and discolored. Fully wash, rinse and sanitize this area. Remove and replace caulking if needed.

FoodCodeText: Calibrate food temperature measuring devices in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as often as necessary to ensure accuracy.
InspectorComments: Food thermometer used to measure temperature of baked and fried foods in the back kitchen area of the deli was off by approximately 27F. Recalibrate thermometer as often as necessary to ensure that it is accurate to +/- 2F. Maintain.

FoodCodeText: Remove all items unnecessary to the operation of the business from the premises.
InspectorComments:
OBSERVED VARIOUS ITEMS IN THE BACK OF THE FACILITY THAT ARE NO LONGER BEING USED DURING DAILY 
BUSINESS OPERATIONS ON SITE. REMOVE ALL ITEMS FROM PREMISES AS THEY CAN CREATE A HARBORAGE AREA 
FOR UNWANTED PESTS.

FoodCodeText: Provide a floor drain, properly grade the floor to drain to the floor drain and properly cove and seal wall/floor junctures when water flushing cleaning methods are used.
InspectorComments:
OBSERVED BASECOVING TO BE MISSING ALONG WALLS IN BACK WAREWASHING AREA AND AT COOKLINE.. INSTALL INTEGRAL 
BASECOVING SUCH AS QUARRY TILE OR STAINLESS STEEL COVING IN THIS AREA.

FoodCodeText: Post a sign at all handwashing sinks used by employees to remind them to wash their hands.
InspectorComments: Provide hand washing signs at all employee hand washing sinks.

FoodCodeText: Remove the supply of individual disposable towels and hand soap from food preparation sinks, utensil washing sinks, and mop sinks.
InspectorComments: Remove the soap and paper towel dispensers installed at 3 comp sink in back prep room.

FoodCodeText: Food service equipment must be certified for sanitation. The certification must be by an American National Standards Institute (ANSI) accredited program.
InspectorComments: The data plate on the 2-door glass cooler indicates it can be used to store only TCS foods in their original package. Discontinue the use of this refrigerator for storing TCS items like shredded chicken and cooked pasta.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Observed cheese and sliced tomatoes in Coldwell at 46*F and 43*F. Maintain all cold TCS foods at 41*F or less. Turn thermostat down on Coldwell to lower ambient temperature to 41*F or less.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution:  • Within the concentration specified in 21CFR.178.1010, and  • According to the manufacturer/'s directions
InspectorComments: Observed 0 PPM quat sanitizer in the 3-comp sink. Provide and maintain 200-400 PPM quat sanitizer in the sanitizing compartment of the 3-comp sink. Note: Utensils in the sanitizing compartment of 3-comp sink were piled so high numerous utensils were at least 4-6 inches above the water line. Maintain water level in sink covering utensils.

FoodCodeText: Use an effective method to date mark refrigerated, ready-to-eat, TCS food prepared and held for more than 24 hours. Day one is the day the food was made.
InspectorComments: Observed shredded chicken and other ready-to-eat foods in 2 door glass cooler that were not date marked. Date mark ready-to eat foods so that they will be used within 7 days.

FoodCodeText: Label all containers of food and food ingredients with their common name.
InspectorComments: Observed unlabeled containers of bulk flour in back prep area. Label containers with their contents.

FoodCodeText: Food businesses must have handwashing sinks with a water temperature of:   • At least 100 degrees F   • Not hotter than 130 degrees F   • If children use the sink, the water temperature must not be hotter than 120 degrees F
InspectorComments: Observed hot water of only 87*F in employee restroom. Provide hot water at hand sink between 110-130*F

FoodCodeText: Keep the plumbing system in good repair.
InspectorComments: The hand wash sink at the deli front counter drains really slow. Unclog sink so that it drains properly.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments: Observed a ServSafe certificate on site, however, unable to verify any employee holds the State issued CFPM credential.  Ensure at least one full time employee has obtained the CFPM credential from the State and post certificate.

FoodCodeText: Hang mops to dry after using. Store mops in a way that will not make walls, equipment or supplies dirty.
InspectorComments: Observed mop sitting in mop bucket inside mop sink in storage mode.  Hang mops to dry after each use.

FoodCodeText: Post a sign at all handwashing sinks used by employees to remind them to wash their hands.
InspectorComments: Observed handwash signage missing from handwash sink in catering kitchen.  Ensure ALL handwash sinks have the proper signage.

InspectorComments: Observed protective wrapping still on the inside of the lowboy cooler and peeling away.  This wrapping creates a surface that is not smooth and/or easily cleanable.   Removed that wrapping.

FoodCodeText: Before using Time as a Public Health Control for TCS food develop, follow and keep written procedures onsite.
InspectorComments: Observed operators using time as a public health control from waffle batter (ingredients contain butter and eggs) They hold batter containers at room temperature and switch out once a shift.   Discussed with person in charge.   Develop written procedures for this practice and keep on site and available for review.

FoodCodeText: Have an item to verify the surface temperature of dishes reaches 160 degrees F inside mechanical hot water dishwashers.
InspectorComments: Establishment has new hot water sanitizing dish machine (not set up at time of inspection) Obtain test strips or device that is capable of measuring plate temperature.

FoodCodeText: Properly cove and seal floor-wall junctures.
InspectorComments: FROM PLAN REVIEW INSPECTION:     ON AND AROUND THE MAIN FLOOR WALK-IN COOLER, BASE COVE IS STILL NEEDED.     INSTALL STAINLESS STEEL BASE COVE STRIPS AROUND WALK IN COOLER.

InspectorComments: MOP WAS STORED INSIDER MOP BUCKET.     PROVIDE AND USE EFFECTIVE WALL MOP HANGERS TO HANG THE MOP SO THAT THE MOP CAN DRIP DRY DIRECTLY INTO THE MOP SINK AND NOT ONTO THE HANDLE OF THE MOP. DO NOT STORE MOPS ON THE FLOOR OR INSIDE MOP BUCKET / SINK.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED OPERATOR TOUCHING READY TO EAT FOOD WITH BARE HANDS (CUTTING TOMATOES).      INSTRUCTED PERSON IN CHARGE TO TRAIN PERSONNEL TO LIMIT DIRECT HAND CONTACT AND TO USE GLOVES OR UTENSILS TO TOUCH READY TO EAT FOODS (E.G: SALADS, GARNISHES, BREAD, CILANTRO, ETC).      INSTRUCTED FOOD WORKER PUT ON GLOVES OR USE DELI TISSUE.

FoodCodeText: Do not store food in locker rooms, toilet rooms, dressing rooms, garbage rooms, mechanical rooms, under unprotected sewer lines, under leaking water lines, under water lines on which water has condensed, under open stairwells, or under other sources of contamination.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED FOOD STORED UNDER WHAT APPEARS TO BE SEWER PIPES.      YOU HAVE TWO OPTIONS:     MOVE FOOD TO ANOTHER LOCATION.      PROVIDE A DROPPED CEILING OR A WAY TO PROTECT FOOD FROM CONTAMINATION COMING FROM PIPES ABOVE.      NOTE: THIS ROOM IS ALSO MISSING PROPER WALLS AND FLOORING.

FoodCodeText: Floors, walls and/or ceiling surfaces are missing. Install smooth, durable, and easily cleanable floor, wall and ceiling surfaces.
InspectorComments: FROM PLAN REVIEW INSPECTION:     IN THE LOWER LEVEL WHERE THE GREASE TRAP WAS INSTALLED, FLOOR AND WALLS ARE BARE.     INSTALL FLOOR AND WALL COVERINGS TO BE SMOOTH AND EASILY CLEANABLE FOR THREE FEET AROUND THE GREASE TRAP.     ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------     OBSERVED FOOD STORED AT TWO LOCATIONS WHERE THERE ARE NO FINISHES FOR FLOOR, WALLS AND CEILING.      STORE FOOD ONLY ON PREVIOUSLY APPROVED LOCATIONS WITH FINISH CEILING, FRP WALLS AND NOT RAW CONCRETE FOR FLOORING.      SEE DOCUMENT ATTACHED FOR GUIDANCE.

FoodCodeText: Post a sign at all handwashing sinks used by employees to remind them to wash their hands.
InspectorComments: HAND WASHING SIGN WAS MISSING AT HAND SINK LOCATED IN THE BAR AND RESTROOM.     PROVIDE A SIGN FOR EACH SINK USED BY FOOD WORKERS.

InspectorComments: CAN OPENER BLADE WAS SOILED AND IN NEED OF CLEANING.     CLEAN AND MAINTAIN CAN OPENER CLEAN.

InspectorComments: SOME FILTERS (BAFFLES) HAD BEEN REMOVED FROM THE KITCHEN HOOD.      REPLACE MISSING FILTERS FOR KITCHEN HOOD.

FoodCodeText: Keep handwashing sinks accessible at all times. Make sure they are only used for handwashing.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED STRAINER SET UP ON HAND WASHING SINK LOCATED IN THE MAIN KITCHEN AND BAR.     THESE SINKS MUST BE USED ONLY FOR HANDWASHING.     PERSON IN CHARGE REMOVE STRAINERS AT BOTH SINKS.     NOTE: IN THE BAR AREA YOU HAVE A DESIGNATED DUMP SINK AND HAND SINK. YOU CAN ALSO DUMP LIQUIDS ON THE 4TH COMPARTMENT LEFT TO YOUR 3-COMP SINK (BAR).

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments: NO STATE REGISTERED CFPM CERTIFICATE AVAILABLE.      GO TO AN APPROVED SERVSAFE CLASS AND THEN SUBMIT DIPLOMA TO MINNESOTA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH.      ONCE YOU RECEIVE YOUR STATE CERTIFICATE, PLEASE POST IT ON A VISIBLE PLACE.      https://www.health.state.mn.us/communities/environment/food/cfpm/index.html

InspectorComments: THE PERSON IN CHARGE DID NOT KNOW ABOUT THE 24 HOURS / SYMPTOM FREE EXCLUSION REQUIREMENT TO RETURN TO WORK FOR EMPLOYEES HAVING BEEN EXCLUDED WITH SYMPTOMS SUCH AS VOMITING AND / OR DIARRHEA, ETC. InspectorComments: OBSERVED FOOD WORKER WITH LONG BEARD PREPARING FOOD WITHOUT HAIR RESTRAIN.     USE BEARD SNOOD OR OTHER TYPE OF HAIR RESTRAINTS DURING FOOD PREPARATION.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must make sure employees follow proper food safety procedures, including:  • Proper handwashing  • Preventing cross-contamination from bare hands  • Proper cooking of TCS foods  • Proper cooling of TCS foods  • Proper hot and cold temperatures of TCS foods  • Preventing plumbing cross connections  • Properly sanitizing equipment and utensils
InspectorComments: ESTABLISHMENT WAS NOT ADEQUATELY EXECUTING ACTIVE MANAGERIAL CONTROL (AMC) WITH MULTIPLE HIGH PRIORITY (IMPORTANT) VIOLATIONS. FoodCodeText: Throw away TCS foods seven days after being made or opened. Day one is the date food was made or opened.
InspectorComments: Multiple example of TCS foods in the walk-in cooler holding beyond 7 days including acidified vegetables. All house prepared TCS foods need to be used or discarded within 7 days of production. If acidified vegetables are desired to be held for more than 7 days a HACCP plan could be pursued as an alternative.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Gumbo was cooling in the walk-in cooler filled to approximately 8 inches of fill depth. Effective cooling methods were reviewed with the manager. When cooling without the help of ice ensure that foods are not filled beyond a depth of 2 inches and remain uncovered until the entire cooling process is complete.

FoodCodeText: Before using Time as a Public Health Control for TCS food develop, follow and keep written procedures onsite.
InspectorComments: Facility is holding multiple TCS foods such as cooked sausage and sauces at room temperature or on ice without any indication of how long the product was been out of mechanical refrigeration. Develop a time marking system, write out those procedures and maintain them on site for training employees.  Reviewed potential ways to do this with the manager.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Multiple hot TCS foods such as cooked beans holding between 115-125 degrees F. Unit temperature turned up during the inspection and hot holding parameters reviewed with the cook. Ensure that all hot TCS foods are holding at or above 135 degrees F.

FoodCodeText: Provide a plumbing system that is designed, constructed, installed, and repaired with approved materials, equipment, and devices complying with chapter 4714 and Minnesota Statutes, sections 326B.43 to 326B.49.
InspectorComments: Multiple hand sinks behind the bar are not in working condition. Valves and other needed parts have been ordered. Ensure that all hand sinks are in working condition.

FoodCodeText: Keep the physical facilities in good repair.
InspectorComments: Grout lines throughout multiple areas in the kitchen are eroding providing deep pockets for moisture and debris to accumulate. Re-grout as needed to provide a smooth floor finish.

FoodCodeText: Store all clean equipment and utensils in a self-draining position that permits air drying and covered and inverted.
InspectorComments: Ice buckets storing on top of the ice machine, one was positioned cup and the other had the lip directly storing on the dusty top of the ice machine. Store these ice buckets in a way that prevents contamination and prevents water from pooling inside them.

FoodCodeText: Clearly label working containers of toxic chemicals with the common chemical name.
InspectorComments: Multiple examples of chemical spray bottles in the dish area without a label. Ensure that all chemical spray bottles are labeled.

InspectorComments: MISSING COVERED GARBAGE INSIDE EMPLOYEE RESTROOM.     PROVIDE A COVERED GARBAGE FOR THIS RESTROOM.

InspectorComments: OBSERVED FEW MISSING CEILING TILES THROUGHOUT THE KITCHEN.     REPLACE MISSING TILES.

FoodCodeText: Keep handwashing sinks accessible at all times. Make sure they are only used for handwashing.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED EQUIPMENT AND FLOOR RUNNER STORED IN FRONT OF HAND SINK (BACK KITCHEN).     DO NOT STORE ANYTHING INSIDE OR IN FRONT OF HAND WASHING SINKS. DO NOT BLOCK ACCESS TO SINKS.     PERSON IN CHARGE CLEARED ACCESS DURING INSPECTION.

BE SURE THE PERSON IN CHARGE CAN LOCATE THE LOG UPON REQUEST BY HEALTH INSPECTORS. A SAMPLE IS ATTACHED TO THIS REPORT.

FoodCodeText: Provide containers for food or beverages prepared for takeout or to be eaten immediately. Containers must be reuseable, recyclable or compostable.
InspectorComments: Observed #6 coffee lids and small covers for condiment cups on site at the time of inspection. Discussed with Person In Charge that these items are not complaint with the City of Minneapolis Green to Go Ordinance as they are not reusable, recyclable or compostable. Will attach most current Green to Go Ordinance in email with report for guidance. Discontinue ordering non-compliant takeaway containers.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments: There was no current Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certified for the establishment at the time of inspection. Discussed requirement with Person In Charge. Will attach initial State of MN application for manager to apply to the State once they pass an approved course. Will provide CFPM information from State of Minnesota to operator in emailed report as well. Obtain CFPM and post certificate in establishment once it is obtained, then maintain current.

FoodCodeText: Launder linens that do not come in direct contact with food between operations if they become wet, sticky, or visibly soiled.
InspectorComments: Wet wiping cloths were observed being used below cutting boards during inspection. Discussed with Person In Charge that this is not an approved use for wet cloths and that once wet, they must be stored in sanitizer solution to be constantly sanitized. Approved ways to stabilize cutting boards, such as rubber mats and rubber stabilized cutting boards were discussed as alternatives to the current unapproved method. Discontinue using wet cloths to stabilize cutting boards and use approved methods.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved chlorine chemical sanitizer solution. The solution must have a minimum concentration of 50 ppm. The solution must also meet the temperature and pH requirements of this rule.
InspectorComments: Chlorine dish machine sanitizer concentration did not measure above 10PPM over 3 separate cycles. Sanitizer concentration is required to be 50PPM minimum according to machine data plate. Discussed with Person In Charge that sanitizer concentration must be at least 50PPM to effectively sanitize. Service dish machine so that it maintains 50PPM chlorine and monitor with chlorine sanitizer test kit. Service as necessary.

FoodCodeText: Provide a written agreement or statement from the supplier stipulating that the fish are frozen to a temperature and for a time as specified in rule.
InspectorComments: Cold smoked salmon served in a raw state as lox menu items did not have parasite destruction records available. Explained Obtain records from supplier and maintain on site for inspector to review during inspections.

FoodCodeText: Have a test kit for the type of sanitizer used.
InspectorComments: There was no chlorine sanitizer test kit available on site to measure sanitizer concentration of low temperature chlorine dish machine. Dish machine was below safe sanitization concentration for chlorine when tested with inspector's chlorine test kit. Provide and maintain a chlorine test kit on site at all times to monitor chlorine dish machine concentration to ensure it is effectively sanitizing dishes.

FoodCodeText: Provide labeling for bulk, unpackaged food, such as bakery treats prepared on the premises of the food establishment or at another food establishment or a food processing plant that is owned by the same person and is regulated by the food regulatory agency that has jurisdiction.
InspectorComments: Bakery items delivered from another establishment that are displayed behind the counter did not have ingredient or allergen information available for customers to see upon request. Provide this information and keep available behind the counter for customers to view if they ask for it. Maintain list current with any new additions.

FoodCodeText: Keep a log to record employee illness symptoms. Have it available upon request.
InspectorComments: There was no means of tracking employee illness at the time of inspection. Discussed with Person in Charge about employee illness training and PIC was knowledgeable in training but did not have method of tracking/recording employee illness occurrences. Will provide employee illness log with emailed report for operator to print out, keep on site and use with each employee illness occurrence/report. Maintain employee illness log on site.

FoodCodeText: Food workers must wash their hands before starting food preparation tasks.
InspectorComments: Food employee was observed scrolling on their personal phone with gloved hands at the Prep Cooler in the Fryer area. When an order was placed, employee removed gloves and put on new gloves without washing hands. Discussed with Person In Charge that employees must wash hands after handling personal food, touching their face or touching other personal items, and each time before working with food. Retrain employees to wash hands before food preparation activities. Monitor and correct employees who deviate from this safe food practice.

FoodCodeText: Have a food thermometer easily available to measure the internal temperature of foods.
InspectorComments: Food thermometer with thin tip was not working at the time of inspection. It was suspected by Person In Charge that it needed a new battery. Provide battery to thermometer so that temperatures can be taken for foods. Maintain thermometer functioning according to manufacturer instructions.

FoodCodeText: Store the food preparation and dispensing utensil in a food that is not TCS food with the handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed such as bins of sugar, flour or cinnamon.
InspectorComments: Scoops were observed stored in bulk flour bin with handle touching the product. Discussed with Person in Charge that scoops need to be stored with handle extended out of the food so that the handle does not potentially contaminate the food. Retrain staff to place scoop with handle extending out of food product and maintain.

FoodCodeText: The consumer advisory disclosure must include either:  • A description of the food as raw or undercooked  • An asterisk to a footnote describing the food as raw or undercooked
InspectorComments: Establishment has an asterisks next to menu items allowed to be served raw or undercooked and a reminder at the footnote of the menu. However, the menu was missing the disclosure stating the food is raw or undercooked. Explained to the MOD the difference between the disclosure and the reminder, and why both are required. Provided the MOD the Minnesota Dept of Health (MDH) factsheet on consumer advisory and informed him to update their menu to include the missing disclosure.

FoodCodeText: Maintain the temperature at the manifold of the hot water sanitizing rinse at a maximum temperature of 194 degrees F (90 degrees C) and no less than 165 degrees F (74 degrees C) for a single tank, stationary rack, single temperature machine or 180 degrees F (82 degrees C) for all other machines.
InspectorComments: The hot-temp bar glass washer's wash and rinse cycles did not hit the minimum water temperature, 150*f and 180*F respectively, required. Informed the MOD to discontinue the use of the bar glass washer until it's serviced and  ensured  to maintain the minimum hot temp required for the wash and rinse cycles.

FoodCodeText: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment must be made of  materials which are corrosion-resistant, non-absorbent, and smooth. Remove equipment with non-food contact surfaces made of other materials.
InspectorComments: - Observed clean bar glasses stored on unfurnished, chipped wood shelves above the bar counter.  Informed the MOD these types of surfaces and exposed woods are not approved for the storage of clean glasses, equipment  and utensils , and establishment must either replace it or discontinue storing clean glasses on these shelves.   - Wood panel attached to the underside of the bar counter above the glass washer must be removed and replaced as it's not smooth and cleanable surface

FoodCodeText: Have an item to verify the surface temperature of dishes reaches 160 degrees F inside mechanical hot water dishwashers.
InspectorComments: Establishment  did not have hot-temp strips or other devices to manually monitor the temperatures of the hot-temp bar glass washer or the kitchen dish machine. Informed the MOD to ensure they have test strips or devices that can enable them to manually monitor the temperatures of the hot-temp bar glass washer or the kitchen dish machine

FoodCodeText: Hang mops to dry after using. Store mops in a way that will not make walls, equipment or supplies dirty.
InspectorComments: Used wet mops were observed stored inside the mop sink. Informed the MOD to consider installing a mop hanger above the mop sink, and to hang the mops to dry above the sink after they're used.

FoodCodeText: For mechanical dishwashing machines using hot water sanitizing, the surface temperature of the utensils and equipment must reach 160 degrees F or higher.

If dishes were needed before machine was repaired, a final sanitize step in immersion of the 3 basin sink will be required. Ensure that the sanitizer range on the directions of the dispenser's container is within safe and effective range. Monitor dish machine more frequently and maintain sanitization temperature at 160F at all times.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Prepped pans of lasagna no deeper than 2 inches were observed sitting on the counter top measuring 64F. When asked, Chef stated that they were preparing the pans of lasagna to be stored in the Walk In Cooler and then cooked for tomorrows lunch service, but was interrupted mid-prep as they were short staffed and he had to help serve. Prep had started 1.5 hours earlier. Discussed with Chef that there were 2.5 hours left in the 4 hour ambient cooling window to get the food cooled to 41F or below safely. Chef opted to place pans on a speed rack and place them in the Walk In Freezer to cool more rapidly. After 30 minutes, temperature of product was measured at 53F. Instructed Chef to continue monitoring cooling every half hour for the remaining hour of cooling to ensure that food reached 41F or below within 4 hours, or the food would need to be discarded. Maintain all cold, TCS foods at or below 41F at all times.

FoodCodeText: Remove frozen fish from the reduced oxygen package prior to thawing under refrigeration or immediately after thawing if using the running water method of thawing.
InspectorComments: Several packages of tuna and tilapia in Reduced Oxygen Packages (ROP) were observed thawing still inside their intact ROP packages. This presents a serious risk of foodborne illness by the bacteria Clostridium botulinum. Inspector and Person in Charge discussed that oxygen stops the growth of this bacteria, so the bags can be cut open on the corner to let oxygen in as soon as they are removed from the freezer.          At the time of the inspection, the fish were below 38F, so they were able to be opened to continue thawing.     Train staff to always open ROP packages of raw fish before thawing to allow oxygen to enter the package.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.
InspectorComments: Employees were observed handling chopped green onions when sprinkling them over cooked dumplings before setting them on the counter for servers to take to the customers. Inspector spoke with Chef and discussed that food that is ready to eat cannot be touched with bare hands as it has a high risk of spreading foodborne illness directly to customers. There were no gloves on the cook line at the time of inspection and when asked where they were, Chef grabbed a box off of the server area and placed it on the cook line.  Bartender was observed cutting limes with bare hands in the bar area. When told that they should not be touching food with bare hands and that they could use gloves, bartender said they did not have any gloves. Inspector instructed them to grab some gloves on the cook line. Inspector verbally went over different methods to avoid touching food that is ready to eat with bare hands, such as gloves, garnish picks, pre-slicing fruit wedges with gloves and then placing them on the glass with tongs, etc. Retrain employees to use gloves, spoons or other methods of adding spices, garnishes to food so that they are not touching food with their bare hands. Discard food that is touched with bare hands.

This was discussed with the Chef and Manager at the time of inspection. Retrain employees on proper handwashing procedures and ensure washing time is long enough to scrub all parts of the hands, wrists and part of the arms.

FoodCodeText: Food workers must wash their hands before starting food preparation tasks.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: On the back countertop, there were 6 deep bus tub type bins of General Tao Chicken that had finished frying at 3:30PM according to the Chef. Each bin of chicken was measured between 78F and 90F at the time of inspection at 6:30PM. Discussed with Chef that foods that are hot need to be cooled from 135F to 70F or below in 2 hours, then from 70F or below to 41F or below in 4 hours. Inspector asked if Chef took any temperatures of the chicken when it was taken off the fryer or at any point after that and Chef had not taken any temperatures of any of the chicken cooling on the counter top. The first critical cooling time/temperature window had been missed, even allowing additional time for the chicken to cool from the fryer. Discussed with owner over the phone the situation and the cooling risks associated with improperly cooled foods that can make people sick and that the chicken cooled in this manner may not be not safe to serve to customers. Owner agreed over the phone to discard the chicken. Took temperatures in the presence of the Manager on site and Chef and relayed the owner's decision to discard. All 6 bins of chicken were observed discarded at that time.  Retrain employees to cool food in shallow containers, under refrigeration, within required time and temperature frames to ensure that food is safely cooled.

FoodCodeText: Provide and maintain a chemical sanitizer generated by a device on site at the food establishment that complies with 7US Code 136 to 136q, 40CFR.152.500 and 156.10, displays the US EPA device manufacturing facility registration number on the device and is operated and maintained according to manufacturer's instructions.
InspectorComments: Sanitizer bucket dispenser in the dish room was observed with a sticker on the dispenser that stated "Quat". When Chef dispensed sanitizer into bucket it was measured with the inspector's quat tape and it was 0PPM at the time. When inspector looked at the chemical hooked up to the dispenser, it was a chlorine in a large 5 gallon bucket. After testing the same bucket with facility's chlorine test strip, it was also measured at 0PPM. After looking around for other available sanitizers, there was commercial bleach available that inspector and chef mixed to 100PPM by mixing one capful of bleach to 4 liters of water. Two buckets were placed on the floor of the cook line to sanitize the cook line. Retrain employees to test sanitizer buckets and refresh them when they are below the minimum chlorine concentration required on the chemical label. Dish machine in the front bar area for washing glasses had an empty jug of chlorine sanitizer and there was no other chlorine sanitizer to replenish it with. It was discussed with front of house Manager that they should not use the dish machine in the front until chlorine sanitizer can be provided to it by the chemical supplier and measures 50PPM available chlorine before using. Retrain employees to monitor dish machine sanitizer levels more frequently so that the machine is adequately sanitizing dishes.

InspectorComments: Tongs were observed stored on oven and fryer door handles at the time of inspection. Instead, tongs can be placed on prep counters, utensil spaces on grills or in buckets, and the utensils are washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours. Chef cleared tongs from the area immediately and placed new tongs on the work surfaces that are able to be cleaned. Retrain staff to keep ready to use and in use tongs on approved surfaces.

Inside of product was still frozen below 32F. Retrain employees on correct thawing methods for raw animal products and employ safe methods.

FoodCodeText: Wiping cloths used for wiping surfaces must:  • Be held in an approved sanitizing solution  • Laundered daily

FoodCodeText: Throw away TCS foods seven days after being made or opened. Day one is the date food was made or opened.

The requirement for the date mark of 7 days is because some bacteria can grow at refrigeration temperatures and make people sick. Retrain staff to date mark sauces made in house for 7 days and use within that time period so that they are safe to serve to customers.

FoodCodeText: Use only chemical sanitizers on food-contact surfaces that meet Title 40, Code of Federal Regulations requirements: • Part 180, section 180.940 • Part 180, subpart E, section 180.2020

FoodCodeText: Have a test kit for the type of sanitizer used.
InspectorComments: There was no bleach sanitizer test kit on site to monitor sanitizer concentrations. Provide one and maintain one on site at all times.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Birria Beef (126F) and Fried Rice (131F) were observed improperly hot held below 135F in the Warming Unit at the time of inspection. Chef opted to discard product 4 hours from time they placed hot food in the warming unit. Discussed with Chef that the warming unit likely needs to be turned up higher so that when the food is added to the unit, it stays hot during service. Retrain staff to monitor temperature of hot held product and ensure that they are 135F at all times or higher. Keep hot TCS foods at 135F or higher at all times.

FoodCodeText: Provide labeling for bulk, unpackaged food, such as bakery treats prepared on the premises of the food establishment or at another food establishment or a food processing plant that is owned by the same person and is regulated by the food regulatory agency that has jurisdiction.
InspectorComments: There was no sheet for ingredient information for the 4 flavors of cookies made in the establishment and kept behind the counter at the time of inspection. Discussed with Chef to provide ingredient requirements so that customers know what ingredients/allergens are in the products should they ask for it. Provide ingredient information broken down to the sub ingredients so that customers are able to find out what ingredients/allergens are in the cookies baked on site. Maintain that list updated with each new addition.

FoodCodeText: Provide containers for food or beverages prepared for takeout or to be eaten immediately. Containers must be reuseable, recyclable or compostable.

Discontinue using these products and order compliant single-use containers for takeaway.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Observed chicken salad at the cold table to be at a temperature of 47 degrees F. It was determined that ice had not been put in the cold table well to keep the food cold. Business was doing a short-term service at a brewery that lasted 4 hours. Business had just removed product from temperature control at their commissary kitchen an hour prior. Business was informed to monitor temperature of chicken salad and either ensure that it remains below 41 degrees F or discard the item within 2 hours. Ensure that Temperature Controlled for Safety (TCS) foods are maintained at or below 41 degrees F to prevent pathogen growth.

FoodCodeText: Handwashing sinks must be located in close proximity to:  • Food and beverage preparation areas  • Food and beverage service areas  • Warewashing areas  • Toilet rooms
InspectorComments: Observed there to be no handwashing sink within a convenient area for use of where this business was set up for service. Employee stated that they would use the handwashing sink in the bathroom, which was down the hall. The importance of having a conveniently located handwashing sink was discussed with Person-In-Charge. Either provide your own portable handwashing sink, or set up for service in an area with a conveniently located handwashing sink to promote proper handwashing by employees.

FoodCodeText: Food employees must wash their hands after: using the toilet; coughing or sneezing; using a handkerchief or disposable tissue; using tobacco; eating or drinking; handling soiled equipment or utensils; caring for or handling service animals or fish in an aquarium, molluscan shellfish or crustacea in a display tank; as frequently as necessary during food preparation to remove soil, contamination, and to prevent cross-contamination when changing food preparation tasks; when switching between working with raw food and working with RTE food; before donning gloves for working with food; and touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean exposed portions of arms.
InspectorComments: Observed employee touch payment system, leave service area to grab ice, and switch gloves without washing their hands. The importance of handwashing for preventing contamination of food products was discussed with Person-In-Charge. Ensure that employees wash their hands when changing tasks, switching gloves, and any other instances listed in the above code.

FoodCodeText: Wiping cloths used for wiping surfaces must:  • Be held in an approved sanitizing solution  • Laundered daily
InspectorComments: Observed there to be no sanitizer bucket for sanitizing non-food contact surfaces for use onsite. Business does their dishes and sanitizes their food contact surfaces at their commissary kitchen. Provide sanitizer onsite for non-food contact surfaces, or borrow sanitizer from the establishment that you are serving at.

FoodCodeText: Have a test kit for the type of sanitizer used.
InspectorComments: Observed business to not have a sanitizer test kit onsite. Ensure that a test kit is provided to ensure adequate concentration of sanitizer for non-food contact surfaces.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must make sure employees follow proper food safety procedures, including:  • Proper handwashing  • Preventing cross-contamination from bare hands  • Proper cooking of TCS foods  • Proper cooling of TCS foods  • Proper hot and cold temperatures of TCS foods  • Preventing plumbing cross connections  • Properly sanitizing equipment and utensils
InspectorComments: Observed multiple risk factors to be present during the time of inspection. It was observed that TCS foods were not kept under proper temperature control, proper handwashing was not being followed, proper sanitizer was not provided during service hours, and there was no thermometer to monitor TCS food temperatures. There was a general lack of food safety practices observed onsite. All of these risk factors and observations were discussed with Person-in-Charge. Ensure that risk factors for foodborne illness are effectively managed and mitigated during times of service.

FoodCodeText: Have a thin-tipped food thermometer easily available to measure the internal temperature of thin pieces of food.
InspectorComments: Observed there to be no probe thermometer onsite to monitor product temperature during service. It was discussed with Person-In-Charge that a probe thermometer is required, as highlighted in the observation that TCS foods were not being held at proper temperature. Ensure that a probe thermometer is available during times of service.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments:
Observed there to be no State of Minnesota Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) to be posted in the meat area. Information for getting this certification will be included in this report. Ensure 
that an employee acquires this certificate and that it is readily available to be reviewed upon inspection.

FoodCodeText: Keep a log to record employee illness symptoms. Have it available upon request.
InspectorComments:
Observed no method of recording instances of employee diarrhea or vomiting onsite. The requirement of recording every 
instance of employee diarrhea or vomiting was discussed with the Person-In-Charge. An employee illness log will be included in 
this report. Ensure that an employee illness log is maintained onsite.

FoodCodeText: Train employees on effective steps to follow for the cleanup of vomit or diarrhea.
InspectorComments: Observed business to not have a written procedure for the clean-up of a vomiting/diarrhea event. Guidelines for the clean-up of these events will be included in this report. Ensure that a written procedure is maintained with the business when in operation and is followed.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Cooked Lobster Stock was observed cooling at 109F and Cooked Arrabiata Sauce was observed cooling at 132F after 30 minutes in the Walk In Cooler. The stock was measured 1 hour later at 102F and the Arrabiata sauce was measured at 112F. Discussed cooling requirement with Person In Charge and that based on the two points of cooling after 1.5 hrs, it was not likely for these two foods to cool to 70F or below within the first 2 hour cooling parameter. Person In Charge had chef use rapid cooling methods to cool the foods within the next half hour. If foods do not make the first cooling window, they can be reheated to 165F and then cooled again using rapid cooling methods, or they can be discarded. Discussed either of these two options for a corrective action for these two foods. These foods were placed in large volumetric containers to cool, which the Chef said is not typical. Retrain staff to cool foods rapidly within 2 hours to 70F or below for the foods to be safe. Cool within time frame specified above.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Cooked sauces were observed cooling in large volumetric containers that did not allow for foods to be rapidly cooled. These containers were switched during the cooling process as the foods were not cooling as rapidly as they needed to to be safe. Use shallow containers to rapidly cool hot foods within 2 hours to 70F or below.

FoodCodeText: Food workers must wash their hands before starting food preparation tasks.
InspectorComments: Employee washing dishes was observed wearing gloves and loading dirty dishes into the machine and then putting away the clean dishes with the same gloved hands. Discussed with Person In Charge that the staff doing dishes should be washing hands before putting away clean dishes and after loading soiled dishes into the machine, otherwise the employees are contaminating the clean dishes. Person In Charge stated that they would retrain the employee as they were new to the job. Dishes that were put away were sent back through the machine to be cleaned again. Ensure all staff are washing hands before putting on gloves, working with food and putting away clean dishes.

Discussed with Person in Charge that in-use utensils cannot be stored in stagnant water because it can grow bacteria. Discussed storing utensils in the container with no water and ensuring that they are washed, rinsed and sanitized every 4 hours. Discontinue storing utensils that are ready to use in a container of water and change procedure. Container was emptied and utensils were run through the dish machine.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.
InspectorComments: Food employee was observed using bare hands to sprinkle salt onto a dessert item that was not going to be cooked before being served. At another time, food employee was observed placing slices of truffles onto a pasta dish with bare hands before being served. Discussed with person in charge that staff should not be touching ready-to-eat foods with their bare hands as that behavior is a major pathway to spread foodborne illness directly to customers. Other staff were using tongs and tweezers to place garnishes onto dishes that were being served to customers, and person in charge stated they would retrain this food employee to use barriers to hands to avoid touching food that is ready-to-eat.  Bartender was observed placing dehydrated garnishes directly into the customer's drinks using bare hands. Discussed with person in charge that tongs/tweezers should be used to handles these ready-to-eat garnishes that are served in the drinks. Use barriers to bare hands when adding garnishes to drinks, and to pre-cut garnishes that will be placed onto the edge of glasses so that tongs can be used. Retrain staff to avoid touching all ready to eat food with bare hands. Discard ready-to-eat food that is touched with bare hands by staff.

FoodCodeText: Food workers must wash their hands before starting food preparation tasks.
InspectorComments: Food employees were observed wearing gloves and putting away clean dishes after loading soiled dishes into the dish machine without washing hands. This is a practice that can re-contaminate clean dishes, and can also spread foodborne illness from customers to staff and other customers who use the dishes next. Discussed using a system where employees are assigned to dirty dishes only, and employees who are assigned to putting away clean dishes only. When there is no ability to have multiple employees doing dishes, employees must wash hands between loading dirty dishes and putting away clean dishes. If gloves are used, gloves must be discarded, hands must be washed and new gloves must be put on to put away clean dishes. Retrain staff in the approved methods and increase employee knowledge of when they should be washing hands after and before certain tasks.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Chicken Pot Pie Soup was observed cooling in a large volumetric cambro container approximately 6 inches deep with an ice wand in the middle of the food. Food was measured at 103F after 1 hour of cooling.  It was unlikely that cooling within 2 hours from 135F to 70F or below would be achieved with this method. Discussed with Manager and Chef that cooling method be changed and showed Chef the best method for cooling in 2 inch metal pans. Directed staff to place the product into the thin pans to allow the product to cool to 70F or below within 2 hours. Change methods of cooling to thin pans so that fast, static cooling can be achieved with less need for monitoring. Retrain staff to employ this method.

Retrain employees so they know to monitor and maintain all hot TCS foods at or above 135F.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.
InspectorComments: Food employee observed preparing and sorting through pistachios with bare hands on a sheet pan. When asked where the pistachios would be used, Chef replied that they would go in a salad that was ready to eat. Discussed with Chef that foods that are ready to eat and are not going to be cooked further cannot be touched with bare hands, as it is at high risk of spreading foodborne illness. Employee immediately discarded pistachios that were touched. Discussed with Chef to retrain all staff to ensure that they are not touching food that is ready to eat with bare hands. Discontinue handling ready to eat foods with bare hands.

FoodCodeText: In food preparation or dish washing areas, employees must not eat, drink from an unapproved container, or use tobacco.
InspectorComments: Food employee was observed sorting pistachios with bare hands on a sheet tray. The employee was observed taking an amount of pistachios and putting them into their mouth with the same bare hand, then they continued sorting pistachios for service. Discussed with Chef and notified employee that this was not a safe practice, as staff can contaminate food with bare hands after touching their mouth. The tray of pistachios was discarded. Discussed with Chef that to correct this issue a discard of the food and washing hands before putting on gloves to work with the rest of the uncontaminated food must be done. Retrain staff to not touch food with bare hands and to not eat food that is going to be served to customers while preparing it. Designate areas for staff to eat and use methods that do not contaminate food when tasting.

FoodCodeText: Cool TCS food prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature within 4 hours to 41 degrees F (5 degrees C) or less.
InspectorComments: Gravy was observed cooling on a shelf and was measured at 90F after 3 hours. Asked Chef if they took any temperatures during cooling and Chef said they did not. Chef reheated gravy to 165F to begin the cooling process again.  Eggrolls were observed cooling out on counter top at 122F, 30 minutes after cooking. Asked Chef the process for cooling eggrolls and they stated that they leave them out on the counter for 1.5 to 2 hours. Asked if Chef monitors temperatures at all during process and they said they did not. After 1 hour, eggrolls were measured at 114F. Discussed with Chef that foods need to cool from 135F to 70F or below in 2 hours, and then 70F or below to 41F or below in 4 hours, to prevent growing harmful bacteria, and that methods for cooling foods needed to change in order to make sure they were safe. Chef moved eggrolls to freezer to cool, as that was their usual method for cooling. Eggrolls were then temped at 1.5 hours at 72F. Retrain employees to employ rapid cooling methods to cool foods so that they are safe for customers. Retrain staff to cool foods within the time and temperature requirements, guidance document provided with emailed report.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: A container of ranch dressing was observed cooling from room temperature in a large volume container in the Walk In Cooler. Discussed with Chef the methods for making the ranch dressing. Chef stated that they use room temperature mayonnaise to make the dressing and they cool it in the large container. This is not an effective method for cooling. Discussed with Chef to retrain staff to pre-chill all products before cooling in a container that size, or if they use room temperature products, to cool in thinner pans for rapid cooling of these foods.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Cooked black beans (48F), roasted red peppers (47F), raw chicken (44F), aioli (48F), and spinach cream (52) in the Saute Cooler were observed cold holding above 41F. Chef stated that they have been having trouble with the cooler maintaining 41F or below and are looking to purchase a new unit to replace this one.  As a temporary measure, include foods placed in the Saute Cooler under the Time as a Public Health Control plan used on site and discard foods every 4 hours since the cooler cannot maintain foods at 41F. Repair or replace unit to maintain foods at 41F or below at all times.  Sour cream (46F) and hummus (46F) were observed cold holding above 41F in the Server Expo. Internal thermometer of the unit indicated a temperature of 50F at the time of inspection. Chef stated the foods were placed there an hour ago, so foods were moved to a unit that could properly cool and cold hold the foods. Discontinue using this unit to cold hold TCS foods.   Maintain all cold, TCS foods at 41F or below at all times.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Asian Buffalo Sauce was observed cooling in the Walk In Cooler at 108F after 1 hour, and then measured at 80F after 1 hour 45 minutes. Explained to Chef that hot foods need to cool from 135F to 70F or below in 2 hours, then from 70F to 41F or below in the remaining 4 hours to cool safely. Based on the rate of cooling, it is unlikely that the sauce will reach 70F or below in the remaining 15 minutes. Chef opted to reheat the sauce to 165F and begin the cooling process again. Recommended spacing the hot pans further apart when cooling on a speed rack to allow better air flow. Retrain staff to space pans further apart.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)

FoodCodeText: Reheat previously cooked, refrigerated, TCS food for hot holding within 2 hours to a temperature of at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C) for 15 seconds.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must make sure employees follow proper food safety procedures, including:  • Proper handwashing  • Preventing cross-contamination from bare hands  • Proper cooking of TCS foods  • Proper cooling of TCS foods  • Proper hot and cold temperatures of TCS foods  • Preventing plumbing cross connections  • Properly sanitizing equipment and utensils

Chef discarded thawed fish immediately. Retrain staff to thaw vacuum seal frozen fish either removed from packaging or by breaking the seal so that it is safe.

Provide a complete consumer advisory so that customers are adequately warned of the risks of consuming raw or undercooked food or ingredients.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Cooked bean salad and cooked mushrooms were observed cooling using improper methods at the time of inspection.  Cooked bean salad was observed cooling in a container deeper than 4 inches at the time of inspection. Discussed with Chef that foods should be cooled in pans with a fill depth of no more than 2 inches.   Cooked mushrooms were observed cooling on a sheet pan on a speed rack. The sheet pans were observed stacked closely together on the speed rack, not allowing air to circulate between each pan effectively. Discussed with Chef that pans that are cooling should be separated enough on a speed rack to allow for adequate air circulation to speed cooling.   Retrain staff to employ effective cooling methods, such as filling pans to no greater than 2 inches and separating pans on cooling racks to allow rapid cooling of foods.

InspectorComments: At the time of inspection, cooked octopus (47F), house made aioli (48F), marinara sauce (45F), cream cheese (43F), cooked lobster (46F) being improperly cold held in the upper part of the Grill Lowboy. Cooked pork (46F), cooked greens (47F) and carrot puree (47F) were also observed improperly cold holding in the lower part of the Grill Lowboy. Most of the foods had been moved there at 3PM and food temperatures had been taken at 5PM.  The carrot puree was in the unit overnight and had not been moved according to Chef. Chef stated that they had been having issues with the cooler keeping food cold and had it serviced last week with little improvement. Since most of the TCS foods are moved there before opening, an alternative using Time as a Public Health Control was suggested until the cooler can be repaired or replaced and food stored in that cooler must be discarded. Food that was measured above 41F was set to be discarded if not used up, 4 hours from the time that the food was placed into the cooler. Maintain all cold TCS food at or below 41F at all times.

FoodCodeText: Remove all items unnecessary to the operation of the business from the premises.
InspectorComments: Observed storage of tools, personal items, and other equipment not related to the food business to be stored in the basement and intermingled with food items. Remove all items that are not necessary for the food business from the restaurant.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Observed grits, cheesy grits, cooked rice, and corned beef in the kitchen stand-up cooler to be at temperatures ranging from 46 - 49 degrees F. Chef stated that the products in the cooler were stored there overnight. It was discussed with the chef that Temperature Controlled for Safety (TCS) foods must be kept at temperatures below 41 degrees F to prevent bacterial growth. Discard all TCS foods in this cooler that have been stored there overnight.    Observed butter to be stored on the countertops at 78 degrees F. Keep butter under refrigeration or develop a Time as a Public Health Control plan.    Ensure that TCS food are kept at, or below, temperatures of 41 degrees F .

FoodCodeText: Clean all physical facilities (floors, walls, ceilings). Keep them clean.
InspectorComments: Observed the walls and the floors along the cookline to be soiled with debris.    Clean these areas and keep physical facilities clean.

FoodCodeText: Clean non-food contact surfaces of equipment. Keep them clean.
InspectorComments: Observed the sides and wheel bearings of the fryers and grills along the cookline to be soiled.   Observed the interior of multiple coolers in the downstairs storage areas to be soiled.    Clean these pieces of equipment and keep them clean.

FoodCodeText: Food employees must wash their hands after: using the toilet; coughing or sneezing; using a handkerchief or disposable tissue; using tobacco; eating or drinking; handling soiled equipment or utensils; caring for or handling service animals or fish in an aquarium, molluscan shellfish or crustacea in a display tank; as frequently as necessary during food preparation to remove soil, contamination, and to prevent cross-contamination when changing food preparation tasks; when switching between working with raw food and working with RTE food; before donning gloves for working with food; and touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean exposed portions of arms.
InspectorComments: Observed employees to handle multiple types of equipment, handle multiple different types of foods, and to switch multiple tasks and switch gloves without washing their hands. Employees were instructed to wash their hands during the inspection. Ensure that employees wash hands in between handling different food types, between switching gloves and tasks, and any other times required by the above code.

FoodCodeText: Provide an approved sanitizing solution for storage of the wet wiping cloths that is free of food debris and visible soil.
InspectorComments: Observed multiple wet wiping cloths to be stored on food prep surfaces. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket when not in use.

FoodCodeText: Store in-use food preparation and serving utensils only on clean, sanitized surfaces.
InspectorComments: Observed tongs to be hanging from the handles of the fryers and grills. Discontinue storing tongs in this way.

FoodCodeText: Provide containers for food or beverages prepared for takeout or to be eaten immediately. Containers must be reuseable, recyclable or compostable.
InspectorComments: Observed styrofoam takeout containers and P.E. lined coffee cups with black plastic lids to be used at the restaurant. These items cannot be recycled. Discontinue use of these products and make sure that all single-use takeout containers are recyclable, as required by the Green-to-Go ordinance.

FoodCodeText: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils must be clean.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed grits and cheesy grits in the kitchen stand-up cooler, as well as a thick soup in a downstairs stand-up cooler, to be at temperatures ranging from 47 - 48 degrees F. These items were date marked days prior to the inspection. When discussed with chef, they stated that they put the grits and soups in thick plastic containers and place them in the walk-in cooler. It was discussed with chef that this is an ineffective way to cool thick food items. It was discussed with chef to place thick food items in shallow pans to ensure that they can cool quickly. These items were discarded.    Cool food items in an effective method.

FoodCodeText: All equipment and components must be in good repair. Keep them maintained to manufacturer's specifications.

Remove all TCS foods from this cooler and discontinue using the cooler until it is repaired. Repair cooler to make sure that it can maintain an air temperature of 41 degrees or cooler.     Repair these pieces of equipment and keep them in good repair.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must be able to demonstrate their knowledge to the inspector of the importance of the following food handling procedures to preventing foodborne disease: handwashing; avoiding cross contamination; avoiding hand contact with ready-to-eat foods; time and temperature requirements for safely refrigerating, hot holding, cooling, and reheating TCS food; hazards of eating raw or undercooked meat, poultry, eggs, and fish; food temperatures and cooking times required to safely cook TCS food including meat, poultry, eggs, and fish; foods identified as major food allergens and the symptoms of an allergic reaction; identification of critical control points in a food service operation and steps to be taken to ensure the points are controlled.
InspectorComments: Based on discussion of the observed violations with the Person in Charge (PIC), the PIC did not know the risks of TCS foods being left in the Temperature Danger Zone. The PIC did not know that even if prepared foods like fried chicken, roasted duck, roasted pork and egg rolls are reheated before service, they can still make customers sick by Bacterial Intoxication if they are left in the temperature danger zone. The bacterial toxins that grow in prepared foods when they are temperature-abused are not destroyed by recooking or reheating.

InspectorComments: Observed employees changing gloves and changing tasks without washing their hands. In fact, throughout the entire inspection, no food employee was observed to wash their hands at all.    Train employees to wash their hands at the times required. See above.     Further observation of failure to wash hands will result in citations (fines).
