FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed two volunteers in separate domestic kitchen spaces not using effective cooling methods for prepared TCS foods.    1) Several dozen hard boiled eggs were being peeling and set in a bowl on the counter. Inspector discussed with the volunteer how they could put the peeled eggs into a cooler or refrigerator a dozen at a time to restart the cooling process. Volunteer began doing so.     2) Several hot pans of stuffing and mashed potatoes were being covered and stacked on the counter top. Inspector discussed with Person in Charge how covering and stacking hot prevents proper cooling. Person in Charge brought pans to cold units and spread them out to cool.     Provide additional training and oversight to volunteers who prepare hot food that will be cooled.          The most effective way to cool hot prepared foods is to spread them out in shallow pans (fill the food two inches deep or less) and place them uncovered, unstacked and spread out in a refrigerator or cooler.     Do not cover or stack foods until they have fully cooled to 41F or below. (The cooling process is typically not going to be completed while volunteers are on site.)

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.

FoodCodeText: Minneapolis food establishments must comply with the food manager certification requirements, as set out in MN Rules, Chapter 4626.2000 to 4626.2525. In support and/or addition to the MN Rules, all persons licensed to operate a food establishment under this chapter (except short-term food establishments) shall at all times employ at least one (1) full time person with supervisory responsibilities (which may be the licensee) who (1) spends a substantial amount of his/her work week at that food establishment, and (2) who has a current Minnesota Department of Health food manager certificate. A large establishment with more than one food preparation and service location under one (1) license, shall have a Minnesota Department of Health certified manager for each location. A new licensee shall provide proof of certification before the facility is approved to open. The licensee shall notify the city when the certified person leaves or terminates employment with the food establishment. A food establishment that no longer employs a certified manager shall employ a certified manager within thirty (30) days. All establishments (except short-term food establishments and those exempted pursuant to rules adopted under the authority of the ordinance) shall maintain up-to-date written policies and guidelines on the premises. These policies and guidelines shall have been approved by the manager of environmental health and shall govern food handling and preparation, sanitation practices and techniques, personal hygiene including handwashing techniques, the prevention of food borne illness through proper receiving, storage, preparation, cooling and reheating of foods, and other related matters. FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Sliced Tomatoes (48F), Shredded Cheddar Cheese (47F), and Scrambled Eggs (46F) were observed improperly cold holding at the time of inspection in the Sandwich Cooler. Foods had been placed there in the morning at least 5 hours earlier. A measurement of the liquid in the pickle tray that had been in the cooler all day measured 48F at the time. Discussed with Chef that the cooler could be malfunctioning as the air blowing from the coolers circulation fan was weak and not very cold.  Shell Eggs (46F), Heavy Cream (468F), Cooked Lobster (48F) and Waffle Batter (47F) in the Drawer Cooler was observed improperly cold holding at the time of inspection. All foods had been placed there in the morning at least 5 hours earlier, except for a new container of waffle batter pulled from the downstairs Walk In Cooler. Discussed with Chef that sometimes there is a switch at the back of the cooler that they can turn the temperature down, or they may need to service the unit if it does not hold foods at 41F or below A temporary fix was provided to operators to use Time as a Public Health Control on the coolers that were not functioning properly at the time of inspection. Foods that would be used up within 4 hours would be placed on the line for use in restaurant operations and then any remaining product would be discarded halfway through the day after 4 hours. Then a new batch of foods that would be used would be placed in the coolers and used the same way as the first batch. No TCS food is to be stored in the units for more than 4 hours and overnight. Use alternative coolers that are holding at 41F or below to store any TCS foods. Repair or replace coolers and only store TCS foods in them when confident that they are holding food at 41F or below.   All TCS foods above 41F at the time of inspection were voluntarily discarded by Chef.

FoodCodeText: "The city council finds that discarded packaging from foods and beverages constitutes a significant and growing portion of the waste in Minneapolis' waste stream. The council further finds that plastic packaging is rapidly replacing other packaging material, and that most plastic packaging used for foods and beverages is nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable. InspectorComments: Chicken wings in individual portions that were previously smoked and cooled completely in the Walk In Cooler were observed being reheated to hot hold in the Upright Warming Unit. Temperatures ranged from 90F to 109F after 45 minutes and were measured again after 1 hour and 15 minutes from 108F to 130F. Temperatures varied widely between the location of the wings in different spots in the warming unit. Discussed with Chef that this was an unpredictable method to reheat wings and it was not known if the warming unit was designed to rapidly reheat foods to hot hold. Chicken wings were moved to the oven to reheat to 165F within the remaining 45 minutes of time they had to reheat.  Ensure that foods are being reheated to 165F within 2 hours and then hot hold product at 135F or higher. Retrain staff to use rapid reheating methods for foods that are cooked, then cooled completely before reheating to hot hold.

Regulation of food and beverage packaging, therefore, is a necessary part of any effort to encourage a recyclable and compostable waste stream, thereby reducing the disposal of solid waste and the economic and environmental costs of waste management for the citizens of Minneapolis and others working or doing business in Minneapolis. The council further finds that plastic packaging is rapidly replacing other packaging material, and that most plastic packaging used for foods and beverages is nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable. The council also finds that the two (2) main processes used to dispose of discarded nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable plastic foods and beverage packaging, are land filling and incineration, both of which should be minimized for environmental reasons. The council therefore finds that the minimization of nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable food and beverage packaging originating at retail food establishments within the City of Minneapolis is necessary and desirable in order to reduce the city's waste stream, so as to reduce the volume of landfilled waste, to minimize toxic by-products of incineration, to make the waste stream less damaging to the environment, and to make our city and neighboring communities more environmentally sound places to live. (89-Or-060,§ 1, 3-31-89; 96-Or-059,§ 1, 6-28-96) "

FoodCodeText: Have an approved chlorine chemical sanitizer solution. The solution must have a minimum concentration of 50 ppm. The solution must also meet the temperature and pH requirements of this rule.
InspectorComments: The dish machine on site was using chlorine as its sanitizer. The sanitizer was tested over multiple cycles and the chlorine concentration measured 0PPM at each cycle. The hot water sanitizing capability was measured in the machine and it did not measure above 156F after 5 cycles. Dish machine was not adequately sanitizing dishes. Discussed with Person In Charge that dishes need to be sanitized in the sink with a chlorine sanitizer at 50-200PPM as a final step and that the dishes should be sanitized in this method until dish machine is repaired and can sanitize dishes. Repair dish machine.

FoodCodeText: Operate and maintain the warewashing machine and its auxiliary components, including the conveyor speed and automatic cycle times, in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications.

Manual for machine shows chemicals to be used in the machine are only a non-chlorinated dishwashing detergent and a rinse aid. Contact service provider to service machine so that it operates as a high temperature dish machine according to the manufacturer instructions. Operate and maintain dish machine according to manufacturer instructions. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Cooked rice for sushi was observed hot held at 102F in the rice cooker during inspection. Chef explained they cook the rice before service, allow it to cool slightly and then they season it for use in their sushi dishes. They purposely keep the rice around 90-100F for the right consistency to make sushi. Discussed with Chefs that cooked rice should be kept hot at 135F or higher or cooled to 41F or below to be safe. Suggested they consider Time as a Public Health Control plan for their rice and discard remaining rice product after 4 hours. Attached Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) plan with emailed report. Either use TPHC 4 hour plan for cooked rice, keep hot at 135F or higher, or cool and keep at 41F or below to maintain safe.

Repair unit, once unit is holding at 41F or below, foods can be moved back to this unit.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Cooked rice for sushi was observed hot held at 109F in the rice cooker during inspection. Chef explained they cook the rice before service, allow it to cool slightly and then season it for use in their sushi dishes. They purposely keep the rice around 90F-100F for the right consistency to make the sushi. Discussed with Chefs that cooked rice should be kept hot at 135F or higher or cooled to 41F or below to be safe. Suggested Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for their cooked rice if they are intentionally keeping it around 100F. Use one of the following methods to serve safe rice:   Use 4 hour Time As a Public Health Control (TPHC) for cooked rice. Complete TPHC plan (attached with emailed report) and keep it available on site for inspectors to review during inspections  Keep cooked rice hot held at 135F or higher  Keep cooked rice cold held at 41F or below

FoodCodeText: Keep the physical facilities in good repair.
InspectorComments: A floor tile was observed missing in the middle of the bar area by the bar entrance behind the counter. Repair and maintain.  There was an uncovered juncture between two FRP panels in the kitchen, that was covered over with duct tape. Replace with the approved FRP juncture and maintain in good condition.

FoodCodeText: Have a thin-tipped food thermometer easily available to measure the internal temperature of thin pieces of food.
InspectorComments: There was no thin-tipped food thermometer available at the time of inspection. Facility occasionally works with raw chicken and beef burgers, so a thin tip thermometer is needed to measure the temperature of thin meats to ensure that they are fully cooked. Provide a thin tipped thermometer and maintain on site at all times.

FoodCodeText: All equipment and components must be in good repair. Keep them maintained to manufacturer's specifications.
InspectorComments: Drain stoppers in both the wash and sanitizer sink basins were not functioning. Owner bought external plugs that could be used temporarily so facility could properly operate in the short term. Ensure that the drain stoppers that are built into the triple sink are repaired.

FoodCodeText: Keep all intake and exhaust air ducts and filters clean.
InspectorComments: Significant build up of grease and dust on the hood baffles. Discussed appropriate cleaning frequency with the owner. Ensure that hood baffles are cleaned on a consistent and regular basis to avoid the accumulation of grease and dust on them.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Cooked chicken butter sauce cooling from the day before still 62 degrees F in center of container and 47 degrees F on the outer edge. This food was discarded and cooling time/temperature parameters were reviewed. Ensure that cooked TCS foods are cooling within the time and temperature parameters defined above.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Cooked TCS foods were cooling in deeply filled in plastic buckets at depths exceeding 18 inches. Reviewed proper shallow pan cooling method with the owner, manager, and cook. Ensure that food is not filled above 2 inches when utilizing the shallow pan cooling method and placed into a refrigeration unit soon after the cooking process is finished. 30-60 minute counter top venting is acceptable if food temperatures don't fall below 135 degrees F in that timeframe.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: Cooked TCS foods were cooling while in covered containers. Reviewed successful cooling methods with the manager. Ensure that cooling foods remain uncovered until fully cooled.

FoodCodeText: Before using Time as a Public Health Control for TCS food develop, follow and keep written procedures onsite.
InspectorComments: Facility is attempting to use time to manage back up portions of numerous hot foods and sometimes if not used they are being placed back into the cooler. Discussed proper use of time as a public health control and am supplying a template with this report. Ensure that written procedures are developed, trained on and proper time control methods are in place before using time as a public health control. Once a product is managed by time it needs to continue to be managed by time and discarded if not sold within 4 hours.

FoodCodeText: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils must be clean.
InspectorComments: Cutting boards, food contact utensils in storage and can opener blade were soiled with food debris and build up. Discussed what and how to clean food contact surfaces with the manager. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained clean when storing.

FoodCodeText: Provide non-food contact surfaces that are free of unnecessary ledges, projections and crevices and are designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning.
InspectorComments: Exterior of cooking equipment and shelves are lined with tin foil and cardboard and are heavily soiled. Remove these liner type materials to expose the cleanable stainless steel surfaces below.

FoodCodeText: Clean non-food contact surfaces of equipment. Keep them clean.
InspectorComments: Exterior of large food containers on rollers, sides of equipment, interior of the walk-in cooler, shelves throughout and handles of equipment soiled with grease, build up and food debris. Clean and maintain clean all non-food contact surfaces.

FoodCodeText: Clean food contact surfaces of cooking and baking equipment, including microwave ovens, at least every 24 hours.
InspectorComments: Interior of microwaves (both) soiled with food splatter, debris and build up. Clean and maintain clean the interior of microwave surfaces.

FoodCodeText: Clean all physical facilities (floors, walls, ceilings). Keep them clean.
InspectorComments: Walls, floors and ceilings throughout the facility are heavily soiled with build-up of grease, food debris and debris. Reviewed appropriate cleaning methods and frequency with the cook. Ensure that all walls, floors and ceiling are clean and maintained cleaned.

FoodCodeText: Use an effective method to date mark refrigerated, ready-to-eat, TCS food prepared and held for more than 24 hours. Day one is the day the food was made.
InspectorComments: In house prepared TCS foods made 1 or more days before storing in the walk-in cooler and upright cooler without date marking. Reviewed date marking expectations with manager and cook. Ensure that all in-house prepared TCS foods that store overnight are date marked and not held beyond 7 days.

FoodCodeText: Have a test kit for the type of sanitizer used.
InspectorComments: Facility was intending to use chlorine as a sanitizer but didn't have a test kit accessible for use. Manager on day 2 found and provided a chlorine test kit. Ensure that test kit for the sanitizers being used are accessible and being used on a routine basis to test concentration of sanitizer.

FoodCodeText: Have hand soap at all handwashing sinks.
InspectorComments: Soap was missing from multiple hand sinks. On day 2 manager and owner had stocked soap at each hand sink. Ensure that all hand sinks have a supply of soap near them.

FoodCodeText: Provide a waste receptacle at each handwashing sink or group of handwashing sinks if disposable towels are used.
InspectorComments: Hand sink near the cooking area had no trash can near it. On day 2 a trash can was present near this hand sink. Ensure that all hand sinks have a trash can near them.

FoodCodeText: Post a sign at all handwashing sinks used by employees to remind them to wash their hands.
InspectorComments: Some of the hand sinks were missing reminder signage near them. Sample poster is being provided with the report. Ensure that all hand sinks have reminder signage near them.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must make sure employees follow proper food safety procedures, including:  • Proper handwashing  • Preventing cross-contamination from bare hands  • Proper cooking of TCS foods  • Proper cooling of TCS foods  • Proper hot and cold temperatures of TCS foods  • Preventing plumbing cross connections  • Properly sanitizing equipment and utensils
InspectorComments: Core food safety issues were not being actively managed on a daily basis including sanitation, cooling methods, time control management, date marking and handwashing. Ensure that the person in charge is actively managing the food safety practices of staff and the facility.

FoodCodeText: Sanitize food contact surfaces before using and after cleaning.
InspectorComments: Dish washing procedures were described as wash, rinse and dry without a sanitizing step after rinse. Reviewed proper dish washing procedures with the staff. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are properly washed, rinsed and sanitized.

FoodCodeText: Keep the plumbing system in good repair.
InspectorComments: Multiple leaky faucets present throughout the facility including hand sinks and prep sink. Reviewed timeframe for plumbing to be repaired. Ensure that all plumbing including the drain stoppers in the triple sink are properly working.

InspectorComments: Facility was observed using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) for TCS (time/temperature control for safety) foods such as pico de gallo, dressings made in house, sour cream sauces and other foods on top of the counter coolers out of temperature control. A cheese sauce was also being used under this plan, and was observed elevated on the grill flat top so that it could soften up before being  heated upon order. There are two coolers on the cook line that are counter coolers with no prep cooler in the top of the unit. The foods are discarded at the end of the night, which can be at least 6 hours depending on the day. Discussed with director that these foods that are being used for TPHC require a written plan under 4 hours, or 6 hours if food remains at 70F or below. Provide written procedures for all foods used under the Time as a Public Health Control plan and keep available on site for inspectors to verify during inspections.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.

Discussed with director and staff that foods that are ready-to-eat must not be touched with bare hands because of the risk of spreading foodborne illness associated with the practice. Retrain staff to use gloves, tongs or other barriers to the hands to prevent bare hand contact.

FoodCodeText: "The city council finds that discarded packaging from foods and beverages constitutes a significant and growing portion of the waste in Minneapolis' waste stream. Regulation of food and beverage packaging, therefore, is a necessary part of any effort to encourage a recyclable and compostable waste stream, thereby reducing the disposal of solid waste and the economic and environmental costs of waste management for the citizens of Minneapolis and others working or doing business in Minneapolis. The council further finds that plastic packaging is rapidly replacing other packaging material, and that most plastic packaging used for foods and beverages is nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable. The council also finds that the two (2) main processes used to dispose of discarded nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable plastic foods and beverage packaging, are land filling and incineration, both of which should be minimized for environmental reasons. The council therefore finds that the minimization of nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable food and beverage packaging originating at retail food establishments within the City of Minneapolis is necessary and desirable in order to reduce the city's waste stream, so as to reduce the volume of landfilled waste, to minimize toxic by-products of incineration, to make the waste stream less damaging to the environment, and to make our city and neighboring communities more environmentally sound places to live. (89-Or-060,§ 1, 3-31-89; 96-Or-059,§ 1, 6-28-96) "

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Pastrami roasts were still being cooled at a thickness of four inches. Pastrami was being wrapped with paper, topped with ice packs and set into the walk in cooler.    This method has not been validated to be effective. To use this method, a log of time and temperatures must be kept for each roast, beginning when outer portions cool to 135F. Sous Chef stated logs were being kept, but observation of log indicated entries on only two days since the routine inspection.      An additional concern is that the ice packs were observed being placed on pastrami well before it entered the temperature danger zone, which will result in bags with warm water at the time the product is actually cooling from 135F to 41F.          Consider cutting the roasts in half to produce two that are only two inches thick; then they could be laid out flat in the walk-in cooler and allowed to cool without time/temperature logging, because the method has been validated as effective.      A Risk Control Plan is being offered as a cooperative effort to control this risk factor of foodborne illness. Risk Control Plan template will be emailed with this report.

This is not an acceptable practice. Discussed with Chef that these foods either need to be kept hot at 135F or higher, or cold at 41F or below under mechanical refrigeration. Discussed with Chef that storing containers in ice in lieu of mechanical refrigeration is not a reliable way to keep foods cold. Store these foods in a cooler and keep these foods under mechanical refrigeration at all times.  Cooked Ribs (46F) and Cooked Lamb Shank (46F) in the lower part of the Grill Cooler, and Scrambled Eggs (47F), Cream Cheese (47F) and Cooked Lobster (70F) in the upper part of the Grill Cooler were observed improperly cold held at the time of inspection. Lobster container was not sized properly to fit in the Grill Cooler and was observed sitting on the top of the unit, which was not allowing cold air to reach the food.   Keep cold TCS foods under mechanical refrigeration at all times. If the Grill Cooler is not maintaining temperature, it should be repaired. If it cannot be repaired, it should be replaced with a functional unit.  A discard time was set for these foods 4 hours from the time the food was removed from temperature control. Maintain all cold TCS foods at 41F or below.

FoodCodeText: "The city council finds that discarded packaging from foods and beverages constitutes a significant and growing portion of the waste in Minneapolis' waste stream. Regulation of food and beverage packaging, therefore, is a necessary part of any effort to encourage a recyclable and compostable waste stream, thereby reducing the disposal of solid waste and the economic and environmental costs of waste management for the citizens of Minneapolis and others working or doing business in Minneapolis. The council further finds that plastic packaging is rapidly replacing other packaging material, and that most plastic packaging used for foods and beverages is nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable. The council also finds that the two (2) main processes used to dispose of discarded nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable plastic foods and beverage packaging, are land filling and incineration, both of which should be minimized for environmental reasons. The council therefore finds that the minimization of nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable food and beverage packaging originating at retail food establishments within the City of Minneapolis is necessary and desirable in order to reduce the city's waste stream, so as to reduce the volume of landfilled waste, to minimize toxic by-products of incineration, to make the waste stream less damaging to the environment, and to make our city and neighboring communities more environmentally sound places to live. (89-Or-060,§ 1, 3-31-89; 96-Or-059,§ 1, 6-28-96) "

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.

A Risk Control Plan will be offered to management to use cooperatively with Health Department to control the risk of improper cold holding of TCS foods. A draft of that plan will be provided with this report. Temperature checks will be conducted twice a day, recorded and a copy of the log will be emailed to inspector weekly. FoodCodeText: Have an approved chlorine chemical sanitizer solution. The solution must have a minimum concentration of 50 ppm. The solution must also meet the temperature and pH requirements of this rule.

FoodCodeText: Have a test kit for the type of sanitizer used.
InspectorComments: Observed no test strips for sanitizer present on site. Provide test strips for sanitizer to comply with above rule.

FoodCodeText: Keep the plumbing system in good repair.
InspectorComments: Observed no running water due to plumbing issue. Vendor was aware and working on getting it fixed. Maintain plumbing system in good repair.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution:  • Within the concentration specified in 21CFR.178.1010, and  • According to the manufacturer/'s directions
InspectorComments: Observed initial concentration of quaternary ammonium sanitizer at 500ppm. Lower concentration to be within 200 and 400 ppm. Vendor corrected by adding water and diluting the concentration.

Could not locate a method to test the internal temperature of the hot water sanitizing dish machine. Obtain:    - a

 -disposable

FoodCodeText: Keep the physical facilities in good repair.

FoodCodeText: Use approved trapping devices or other means of pest control when pests are found.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED FRUIT / DRAIN FLIES IN THE KITCHEN, SPECIALLY BY MOP SINK, WATER HEATER AND DRY STORAGE ROOM.     CONTACT YOUR PEST CONTROL COMPANY TO ADDRESS AND ELIMINATE FLIES.     HAVE INVOICES AVAILABLE FOR REVIEW BY THE HEALTH INSPECTOR.

FoodCodeText: Have enough handwashing sinks for convenient use by employees.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED FOOD WORKER MIXING DRY INGREDIENTS INSIDE THE DRY STORAGE ROOM.     DRY STORAGE ROOM IS NOT SET UP FOR FOOD PREPARATION. DISCONTINUE ANY FOOD PREPARATION INSIDE THIS ROOM.     SUBMIT FOOD PLANS TO CONVERT THIS AREA FOR FOOD PREPARATION INCLUDING ADDING A NEW HAND WASHING SINK.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: OBSERVED ONE CONTAINER TIGHTLY COVERED OF COOKED BEANS BALLS. FOOD WAS REGISTERING 62F. FOOD WAS RECENTLY MADE.     NO COOLING CURVE LOG WAS AVAILABLE FOR THIS FOOD.      DO NOT COVER / WRAP TCS FOOD DURING COOLING.     PIC REMOVED PLASTIC COVERING.      COOLING HANDOUTS AND INFORMATION IS ATTACHED TO YOUR EMAIL.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Observed ramen noodle dish at 106 degrees F. Staff instructed to stop selling this food item and dispose of leftovers.  Keep all hot holding TCS foods at 135 degrees F or higher.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must ensure only authorized persons are permitted in food preparation, food storage, and warewashing areas of the establishment.
InspectorComments: Observed two children in food prep and storage areas.  Only allow employees necessary for food service in food prep and storage areas.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved chlorine chemical sanitizer solution. The solution must have a minimum concentration of 50 ppm. The solution must also meet the temperature and pH requirements of this rule.
InspectorComments: Observed sanitizing wipes with fragrance. Replace with chlorine sanitizer approved for use on food surfaces.

FoodCodeText: Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods.
InspectorComments: Observed raw ground beef stored about breadcrumbs in fridge.  Keep foods with a higher minimum cook temperature (155 degrees F for ground beef) stored below ready-to-eat foods or foods with a lower cook temperature (such as breadcrumbs or produce) to prevent cross-contamination.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Cabbage tested at 50 degrees F and raw ground beef tested at 48 degrees F. Turn cooler to a lower temperature setting and keep cold foods at 41 degrees F or below.

FoodCodeText: The business license must be posted where it can be easily seen.
Provide a written agreement or statement from the supplier stipulating that the fish are frozen to a temperature and for a time as specified in rule.
InspectorComments: No paperwork from the fish supplier showing evidence of parasite destruction by freezing.  Obtain and send a copy to the health department and keep a copy on site at all times.

FoodCodeText: Keep a log to record employee illness symptoms. Have it available upon request.
InspectorComments: No illness log was available at the time of the inspection.  One was left with the operator.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments: Take a food safety class and send in your certificate to the MDH to obtain a CFPM.  Post a copy in the business.

FoodCodeText: Provide containers for food or beverages prepared for takeout or to be eaten immediately. Containers must be reuseable, recyclable or compostable.
InspectorComments: Observed black plastic takeout containers. These are not recyclable in Minneapolis. For recyclable plastic use only plastics that are #1,2, or 5 and not black. See our Green to Go website for more information:    https://www.minneapolismn.gov/business-services/business-assistance/run/food-business-rules/green-to-go/

FoodCodeText: Keep clean utensils that are unwrapped in trays and holders with their handles up.
InspectorComments: Observed plastic forks, spoons and knives for customer service stored with handles down and utensil portions up. Do not store this way as they become contaminated when customer reach for them.      Had staff rearrange utensils so that the handles were up.

FoodCodeText: Clean surfaces contacting non-TCS foods:  • When surfaces may have been contaminated  • At least once every 24 hours for consumer self-service utensils  • Before restocking consumer self-service equipment and utensils  • As often as needed to keep surfaces clean
InspectorComments: Soda gun drip cups and nozzles were observed soiled with slime buildup. Clean and sanitize drip cups and nozzles according to manufacturer's instructions. Retrain staff to properly clean and clean more frequently to sight and touch.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Melted butter was hot held at 106F on the grill at the time of inspection. Discussed with Chef that butter needs to be kept at 135F or higher to be safely hot held. Chef raised the temperature on the grill top and moved butter to warmer spot to heat up to 135F. Retrain staff to hot hold melted butter at 135F or higher at all times.

FoodCodeText: Keep a log to record employee illness symptoms. Have it available upon request.
InspectorComments: There was no employee illness log available for recording employee illness occurrences at the time of inspection. Provided an employee illness log with emailed report. Keep an employee illness log on site and fill out with each employee illness occurrence. Have available for inspectors to review during inspections.

FoodCodeText: Remove frozen fish from the reduced oxygen package prior to thawing under refrigeration or immediately after thawing if using the running water method of thawing.
InspectorComments: Tuna was observed thawing in the prep sink with the vacuum seal intact. Tuna was still cold, so Chef was instructed to break the air seal on the packages for proper thawing. Retrain staff to break seal of vacuum packaged fish before thawing so that it thaws safely.

FoodCodeText: Store all clean equipment and utensils in a self-draining position that permits air drying and covered and inverted.
InspectorComments: Containers were observed stacked wet so that they could not air dry. Retrain staff to allow containers to fully air dry after being washed, then they can be stacked.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution:  • Within the concentration specified in 21CFR.178.1010, and  • According to the manufacturer/'s directions
InspectorComments: The 3-compartment sink initially had a sanitizer solution of only 100ppm quaternary ammonium.    Sink was emptied and refreshed to 200ppm quaternary ammonium.     Ensure staff refresh solution as needed to maintain 200-400ppm.

FoodCodeText: Discontinue removing shellstock tag or labels from original container until the container is empty.
InspectorComments: Oyster tags were not being maintained with the shell stock.    Keep the tag with its respective shell stock until used up.

FoodCodeText: Record the date on the tag or label from the original container when the last shellstock from it is sold or served.
InspectorComments: Oyster tags were not being date-marked with the last day the shell stock was used up.    Write the date of last use on the tag before adding it to the chronological record system; this is required for trace-back / trace-forward during outbreak investigations such as Vibrio and Norovirus.

FoodCodeText: The reservoir for the produce fogger must be maintained and cleaned in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications, or at least once a week.
InspectorComments: No information on how frequently the produce fogger is cleaned was available.    Clean weekly unless manufacturer specifies otherwise.

FoodCodeText: Clean the reservoir of the produce fogger at least once weekly by: 1. draining and completely disassembling the water and aerosol contact parts; 2. brush cleaning the reservoir, aerosol tubing, and discharge nozzles with a suitable detergent solution; 3. flushing the entire system with water to remove the detergent solution and particulate accumulation; and 4. rinsing by immersing, spraying, or swabbing the reservoir, aerosol tubing, and discharge nozzles with an effective sanitizing chemical per manufacturer's recommendations.
InspectorComments: No information on method for how the produce fogger is cleaned was available.     Clean using the above guidance unless manufacturer specifies otherwise.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments: There is not yet a Minnesota Certified Food Protection Manager onsite, but several managers/employees are scheduled to take the exam next week.    When class certificates are received, at least one manager/employee must apply online to Minnesota Department of Health to become state-registered. This can only be done within the first six months of passing the exam.    Find the online process at:  https://www.health.state.mn.us/communities/environment/food/cfpm/howto.html

FoodCodeText: Wash food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils to effectively remove or loosen soils.
InspectorComments: The clean-in-place pieces of the meat and cheese slicers in the deli were only sanitized, without first washing and rinsing their food contact surfaces.    Discussed with persons in charge and employees that those pieces must also be washed, then rinsed, then sanitized. Check the manufacturer's instructions. If those cannot be found, wash with detergent solution and clean cloth, rinse with water from a spray bottle, then sanitize the clean, rinsed surfaces with solution from spray bottle.

FoodCodeText: All food must be from approved sources.
InspectorComments: Bakery is reselling gluten free and dairy free bread products from Mixin It Up, Sauk Rapids. No record of this company having a wholesale license has been found.    Discontinue purchasing product from this source until they have obtained a wholesale license (from Minnesota Department of Agriculture).

FoodCodeText: Throw away TCS foods seven days after being made or opened. Day one is the date food was made or opened.
InspectorComments: Sliced deli meat was being used to make sandwiches which were packaged and dated to sell by more than seven days after the meat package itself was opened.    Ensure the sandwiches are date marked to be discarded at the end of the seventh day after the meat or cheese they contain was opened.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must notify the regulatory authority of any complaint from a consumer having or suspected of having diarrhea or vomiting, norovirus, hepatitis A virus, Salmonella spp., Shigella spp., Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, or other enteric bacterial, viral, or parasitic pathogens.
InspectorComments: Per discussion, a policy was place that allowed the corporate food safety contact to determine whether a customer complaint of illness should be reported to the Minnesota Department of Health or not.    Correct this policy to ensure that every customer complaint of illness (vomiting or diarrhea) is automatically reported to Minnesota Department of Health.     Report by calling 1-877-FOOD-ILL or directly online at:  https://www.health.state.mn.us/diseases/foodborne/reporting.html

FoodCodeText: Remove frozen fish from the reduced oxygen package prior to thawing under refrigeration or immediately after thawing if using the running water method of thawing.
InspectorComments: Observed thawed fish in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) in prep cooler. Ensure ROP fish are removed from packaging prior to being thawed.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed chicken soup cooling thickly stacked in the container and covered in plastic wrap. Ensure proper cooling methods are being practiced. At time of inspection discussed with PIC, food worker placed chicken soup in a large container where the food was no more than 2 inches deep.

FoodCodeText: For mechanical dishwashing machines using hot water sanitizing, the surface temperature of the utensils and equipment must reach 160 degrees F or higher.
InspectorComments: Observed temperature of the plate inside hot-water sanitizing dish machine at bar reached 145F. Ensure hot-water sanitizing dish machine is sanitizing properly. PIC was told to discontinue using machine until repaired. Dish machine in kitchen is testing at 100PPM chlorine, and all bar wear should be brought to the kitchen to be properly sanitized.

FoodCodeText: Have an item to verify the surface temperature of dishes reaches 160 degrees F inside mechanical hot water dishwashers.
InspectorComments: Observed no maximum registering temperature device on site. Ensure there is one available to properly measure the dish temperature in a hot-water sanitizing machine.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments:
Observed no one with the Minnesota Department of Health Certified Food Protection Manager certificate. Ensure someone with 
the ability to oversee and direct food workers and food activity has the Minnesota Food Protection Manager Certificate and it is 
posted on site

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments:
Observed no one with the Minnesota Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) Certificate. Ensure at least one person who 
oversees daily food safety operations obtains and posts the Minnesota CFPM certificate.

FoodCodeText: Post a sign at all handwashing sinks used by employees to remind them to wash their hands.
InspectorComments: Observed missing handwashing sign at upstairs hand sink to remind employees to wash their hands. Ensure sign is posted

FoodCodeText: Provide control of pests by routinely: • Inspecting incoming food shipments   • Inspecting the premises for evidence of pests   • Eliminating conditions that attract pests
InspectorComments: Observed mouse droppings in basement food prep and storage areas. Ensure pests are eliminated and droppings are cleaned to monitor pest activity.

FoodCodeText: The services of a licensed pest control operator shall be required when a facility has evidence of rodent or insect activity to the extent that rodent droppings are visible, or live insects are seen during an inspection. The facility shall maintain records of the pest control operator's services on file for inspection. (2003-Or-023, ? 3, 2-28-03)
InspectorComments:
Observed no invoice or records for pest control operator, and observed mouse droppings in basement prep and storage areas. 
Ensure licensed pest control operator is being utilized to prevent pests.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Observed reach-in cooler in basement was holding time/temperature controlled for safety (TCS) foods above 41F, batters tested between 50F-60F, air at 57F inside unit. Ensure TCS foods are kept at 41F and below to prevent pathogen growth. Discussed with PIC at time of inspection. PIC discarded TCS foods from the cooler.

FoodCodeText: All equipment and components must be in good repair. Keep them maintained to manufacturer's specifications.
InspectorComments: Observed reach-in cooler in disrepair. Ensure all equipment is maintained in good repair and proper adjustment.

FoodCodeText: Food businesses must have handwashing sinks with a water temperature of:   • At least 100 degrees F   • Not hotter than 130 degrees F   • If children use the sink, the water temperature must not be hotter than 120 degrees F
InspectorComments: Observed hand washing sink tested at 145F. Ensure hand washing sink is no more than 130F to prevent scalding.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Foods in all refrigeration units were above 41F, with Person in Charge reporting that product had warmed while waiting for power to be provided at the event.    Discussed with Person in Charge ways that staging time can be decreased, and that the generator should be used to power refrigeration units while waiting for electric power at events.          Additionally, a large amount of pre-smoked turkey legs were found held in insulated coolers with some ice. TCS foods may not be stored in insulated containers; they must be stored under mechanical refrigeration.     Turkey legs were observed around 52F - 54F. Based on discussion of when the product had been removed from mechanical refrigeration, the legs were not discarded. They were moved immediately - some to reheat in the truck's oven, some to chill in the chest freezer spread out in single depth.          Further observation of TCS foods at such elevated temperatures may result in citations (fines) and administrative actions such as limiting menu.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: Observed pierogi in hot holding at only 125F.    Person in Charge turned the unit up to reheat the product.

FoodCodeText: Provide overhead protection for outdoor servicing areas.
InspectorComments: Numerous boxes of food, a chest freezer and two large insulated coolers were set outside the truck without overhead protection.    When setting up at events where items may be stored outside the truck, provide overhead protection.

FoodCodeText:
Store all food: 
• In a clean, dry location
• At least 6 inches above the floor
InspectorComments: Numerous boxes of food and two large insulated coolers were set directly on the grass outside the truck.     When setting up at events where items may be stored outside the truck, provide flooring material and store food six inches up.

FoodCodeText: Wiping cloths used for wiping surfaces must:  • Be held in an approved sanitizing solution  • Laundered daily
InspectorComments: Wiping cloths found stored in the sanitizer bucket with low sanitizer concentration. Note: PIC replaced the sanitizer solution with concentration of 200 PPM for correction.

FoodCodeText: Post a sign at all handwashing sinks used by employees to remind them to wash their hands.
InspectorComments: Hand washing signage missing from the hand sink in the back kitchen area. Note: Provide it as required.

FoodCodeText: Have an item to verify the surface temperature of dishes reaches 160 degrees F inside mechanical hot water dishwashers.
InspectorComments: No irreversible registering temperature indicator device or T-stick provided for measuring the rack surface temperature of the mechanical dishwasher. Note: Provide & use it as required.

FoodCodeText: Keep the physical facilities in good repair.
InspectorComments: Observed damaged ceiling tiles above the service line areas. PIC stated that was due to the condensation from the pipe inside the ceiling. Note: Technicians seen onsite to work on it.

FoodCodeText: Dispose of condensate drainage, no sewage liquids and rainwater from the point of discharge to disposal  according to Minnesota Pollution Control Agency Rules Chapters 7080, 7081 and 7083
InspectorComments: The beverage draining tubes were not going directly into the floor drain. Fix.

FoodCodeText: In food preparation or dish washing areas, employees must not eat, drink from an unapproved container, or use tobacco.
InspectorComments: Open employee beverages were found throughout the facility. Provide covered containers.

FoodCodeText: Protect food from cross-contamination by using packages or covered containers.
InspectorComments: Items in the side stand up cooler and the walk-in cooler that were not cooling were left uncovered. Cover to protect food.     There were open containers of cut vegetables stored directly on top of other containers of uncovered food. Discontinue.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.
InspectorComments: Observed an employee using barehand contact when making spring rolls. Discontinue. Use gloves or other effective means.

FoodCodeText: Keep all intake and exhaust air ducts and filters clean.
InspectorComments: The hood filter/baffles had a large amount of grease build up. Clean.

FoodCodeText: Prevent grease or condensation from exhaust ventilation hood systems from draining or dripping onto food, equipment, utensils, linens, single-service articles, and single-use articles.
InspectorComments: The hood canopy had grease dripping. Clean.

FoodCodeText: Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods.
InspectorComments: Raw eggs in the 2nd prep line cooler and raw chicken in the 3rd prep line cooler were stored directly about vegetables and egg rolls. Discontinue. Store raw products on the bottom shelf.     The raw products were moved and corrected.

FoodCodeText: Food employees must wash their hands after: using the toilet; coughing or sneezing; using a handkerchief or disposable tissue; using tobacco; eating or drinking; handling soiled equipment or utensils; caring for or handling service animals or fish in an aquarium, molluscan shellfish or crustacea in a display tank; as frequently as necessary during food preparation to remove soil, contamination, and to prevent cross-contamination when changing food preparation tasks; when switching between working with raw food and working with RTE food; before donning gloves for working with food; and touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean exposed portions of arms.
InspectorComments: Observed employees putting on gloves without washing their hands before. Employee must wash their hands before putting on gloves.

FoodCodeText: Clean all physical facilities (floors, walls, ceilings). Keep them clean.
InspectorComments: The floors throughout the kitchen had grease and dirt build up. Deep clean.

FoodCodeText: Discontinue storing food preparation or dispensing utensils in a container of water that is not maintained at 135 degrees F (57 degrees C) and not cleaned when empty.
InspectorComments: The facility was storing in-use utensils in a bin of water. The water was at room temperature and not held at 135 F or higher. If the facility wants to use water, store in water that maintains 135 F or higher.

FoodCodeText: Store in-use food preparation and serving utensils only on clean, sanitized surfaces.
InspectorComments: Tongs were observed being stored on the oven handles. Discontinue and store in a clean location.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: Observed the facility cooling cream cheese wontons completely covered in the walk-in cooler. Store uncovered to allow the product to provide maximum heat transfer.

FoodCodeText: Label and locate  personal medications in areas that do not contaminate food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles.
InspectorComments: Observed a bottle of primrose pill bottle were stored with food in the back dry storage rooms. The bottle was moved away from food areas.

FoodCodeText: Have an item to verify the surface temperature of dishes reaches 160 degrees F inside mechanical hot water dishwashers.
InspectorComments: The facility could not find their high temperature dish machine indicators. Provide to ensure the internal temperature of the dish machine is reaching temperature.

FoodCodeText: Have a food thermometer easily available to measure the internal temperature of foods.
InspectorComments: The facility could not locate their food thermometer. Provide and use.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: The following items were measured above 41 F:  -Sprouts 48 F at room temperature near the wok.   -Cream 43 and 44 F at the bar refrigerator.      Lower units and store sprouts in the cooler.      Sprouts moved to the refrigerator and cream moved to a cooler that was maintaining temperature.

FoodCodeText: Store single-service and single-use items in a clean dry location. All items must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor.
InspectorComments: Boxes of single service items were stored directly on the floor. Store off the ground.

FoodCodeText: Wiping cloths used for wiping surfaces must:  • Be held in an approved sanitizing solution  • Laundered daily
InspectorComments: Observed multiple in-use wet wiping cloths in meat market prep room.  All in-use wiping cloths must remain in a sanitizer bucket.

FoodCodeText: Thaw TCS food by one of the following methods:  • Inside a refrigerator  • Kept completely under running water of 70 degrees F or less. The food must remain at 41 degrees F or less.  • In a microwave oven  • As part of the cooking process
InspectorComments: Observed frozen ground beef thawing in 3-compartment sink at room temperature.  Person In Charge was instructed to thaw food under cold running water.   Ensure that one of the methods listed above is used when thawing food.   Violation was corrected on-site.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed cilantro lime rice in a large plastic food bin located in the walk-in cooler.  According to the Person In Charge, the rice was placed in the large plastic bin during cooling process.   To ensure proper cooling, all food must be placed in shallow pans no more than 4 inches thick or follow one of the passive or active cooling methods.  More information has been provided with the report.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Observed cilantro lime rice cooling from the day before with a middle temperature of 47F and an edge temperature of 41F. Rice had been placed in a large plastic food bin with a lid. TCS food did not meet the cooling parameters and was discarded. Ensure that all TCS foods are cooled rapidly to prevent the growth of bacteria or formation of toxins.

FoodCodeText: Protect unpackaged food from environmental sources of contamination during preparation.
InspectorComments: 1. Observed cut lettuce being washed in one of the compartments of the 3-comp sink.  2. Observed a large frozen ground beef casing thawing in one of the compartments of the 3-comp sink.   Food needs to be protected from possible contamination while thawing or being prepped.   Use 2-comp sink as instructed or wash and sanitize the 3-comp sink before use.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: Observed cilantro lime rice in a large plastic bin, covered with a lid holding large droplets of condensation.  Person In Charge mentioned that food was covered during the cooling process.   All food must be left uncovered during cooling.

FoodCodeText: Use only chemical sanitizers on food-contact surfaces that meet Title 40, Code of Federal Regulations requirements: • Part 180, section 180.940 • Part 180, subpart E, section 180.2020
InspectorComments: Observed a chlorine sanitizer bucket in the deli area with a concentration higher than allowed.  The Person In Charge was able to correct the concentration during the inspection.    Chlorine sanitizer must be maintained between 50-200 PPM. Use the chlorine test strips to verify proper concentration.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: The chicken in the back 2 door cooler was at 54F.  The cooler did not appear to be working.  It was going to be cooking immediately.  (The vegetables in the cooler were not a concern) The 2 door cooler near the grill had several foods that were at 47F.  A number of food items had just been prepared and put in the cooler and may have elevated the temperature of the food.  The operator will check the temperature after some time and more the foods to the other working cooler if necessary and have the unit repaired if necessary.

FoodCodeText: All equipment and components must be in good repair. Keep them maintained to manufacturer's specifications.
InspectorComments: The back tall 2 door cooler does not appear to be working.  The air temp read 57F and all of the items in it were around that temperature.  If foods that need to be refrigerated are to be stored in this, the unit needs to be repaired.

FoodCodeText: Label all containers of food and food ingredients with their common name.
InspectorComments: The bulk containers of sugar, flour, etc. are still not labeled with their common name in the languages used by the staff.

FoodCodeText: The business must employ at least one valid Minnesota Food Protection Manager's certification (CFPM). Find more information on the Minnesota Department of Health web page.
InspectorComments: Have at least one employee take a food safety class to become a CFPM and post a copy of the license in the restaurant.

FoodCodeText: Keep a log to record employee illness symptoms. Have it available upon request.
InspectorComments: No employee illness log was being used at the time of the inspection. Template in English, Somali, and Spanish were left with the operator.

FoodCodeText: The person in charge must make sure employees follow proper food safety procedures, including:  • Proper handwashing  • Preventing cross-contamination from bare hands  • Proper cooking of TCS foods  • Proper cooling of TCS foods  • Proper hot and cold temperatures of TCS foods  • Preventing plumbing cross connections  • Properly sanitizing equipment and utensils
InspectorComments: When discussing food temperatures and sanitation with employees, it did not seems that they did not know the proper hot holding, cold holding, and cooling temperatures for the proper concentration of the sanitizer in the 3 compartment sink.  Employees need to be trained in food safety.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)
InspectorComments: The chicken in the hot holding unit was at 102F.  This side of the unit had been turned off but was turned back on immediately.

FoodCodeText: When utensils are stored in food, keep the handles stored above the level of the food to prevent contamination.
InspectorComments: The ice scoop was laying in the ice with the handle in direct contact with the ice.  It was immediately taken out and set on a tray instead.

FoodCodeText: Store in-use food preparation and serving utensils only on clean, sanitized surfaces.
InspectorComments: A knife was stored in the crack where the lid closes on the prep table where it could be contaminated with dust/dirt.  It was immediately taken out and set on the prep table counter.

FoodCodeText: Separate raw animal foods from ready-to-eat foods.
InspectorComments: Eggs were observed stored above vegetables in one of the back coolers.  These need to be stored below ready to eat foods.

FoodCodeText: "The city council finds that discarded packaging from foods and beverages constitutes a significant and growing portion of the waste in Minneapolis' waste stream. Regulation of food and beverage packaging, therefore, is a necessary part of any effort to encourage a recyclable and compostable waste stream, thereby reducing the disposal of solid waste and the economic and environmental costs of waste management for the citizens of Minneapolis and others working or doing business in Minneapolis. The council further finds that plastic packaging is rapidly replacing other packaging material, and that most plastic packaging used for foods and beverages is nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable. The council also finds that the two (2) main processes used to dispose of discarded nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable plastic foods and beverage packaging, are land filling and incineration, both of which should be minimized for environmental reasons. The council therefore finds that the minimization of nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable food and beverage packaging originating at retail food establishments within the City of Minneapolis is necessary and desirable in order to reduce the city's waste stream, so as to reduce the volume of landfilled waste, to minimize toxic by-products of incineration, to make the waste stream less damaging to the environment, and to make our city and neighboring communities more environmentally sound places to live. (89-Or-060,§ 1, 3-31-89; 96-Or-059,§ 1, 6-28-96) "

FoodCodeText: "The city council finds that discarded packaging from foods and beverages constitutes a significant and growing portion of the waste in Minneapolis' waste stream. Regulation of food and beverage packaging, therefore, is a necessary part of any effort to encourage a recyclable and compostable waste stream, thereby reducing the disposal of solid waste and the economic and environmental costs of waste management for the citizens of Minneapolis and others working or doing business in Minneapolis. The council further finds that plastic packaging is rapidly replacing other packaging material, and that most plastic packaging used for foods and beverages is nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable. The council also finds that the two (2) main processes used to dispose of discarded nondegradable, nonreturnable and nonrecyclable plastic foods and beverage packaging, are land filling and incineration, both of which should be minimized for environmental reasons. FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: A large portion of cooked ground beef was observed in the walk-in cooler which had not been cooled by effective means.    The beef was approximately eight inches deep in a large hotel pan.          Discussed using the Set & Forget method to effectively cool such prepared foods: After initial heat vents from the cooked food, spread the food out in shallow pans so it is not more than two inches deep. Put the pans in a cooler, uncovered, with at least two inches of air space around them. This method has been validated to produce effective cooling, so staff do not have to measure times and temperatures during cooling. When the food is all the way cooled several hours later (41F or less), the food can be covered, or combined into larger contains and then covered. Train staff to use effective cooling.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Ducks were observed being left hanging at room temperature for over three hours to cool. This is not an effective method for safe cooling.    Inspector and Person in Charge discussed a method for safe cooling:         1) Hang roasted ducks in the front display area to cool (and cut from for service) for about 30 minutes.     2) Begin taking regular temperature of ducks until they cool close to 135F.     3) Around 135F, cut the ducks in half and spread on sheet trays so the halves are not touching    4) Immediately move the sheet trays to the cooler.     5) Do not cover until the ducks are fully cooled to 41F.

FoodCodeText: Food employees must wash their hands after: using the toilet; coughing or sneezing; using a handkerchief or disposable tissue; using tobacco; eating or drinking; handling soiled equipment or utensils; caring for or handling service animals or fish in an aquarium, molluscan shellfish or crustacea in a display tank; as frequently as necessary during food preparation to remove soil, contamination, and to prevent cross-contamination when changing food preparation tasks; when switching between working with raw food and working with RTE food; before donning gloves for working with food; and touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean exposed portions of arms.
InspectorComments:
Observed employees changing gloves without washing hands and one employee putting gloves on to cut cooked duck without 
first washing hands. During the entire inspection, no employees were observed to wash their hands.    Train employees to wash their hands at the times required above.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Whole roasted ducks which had been hung up at room temperature shortly after 11:00am. A half duck was observed at 87F at 1:50pm. A whole duck was observed at 105F at 1:55pm.    It is not known exactly what time the ducks reached 135F, because temperatures were not taken and cooling was not monitored.     It is highly likely that the ducks had already been in the temperature danger zone for more than two hours without reaching 70F.     With no Person in Charge present, Inspector directed that ducks be discarded to prevent bacterial intoxication. Employees rather moved ducks to a container in the back of the walk-in cooler, and later brought one to the oven for partial reheating and service.     At that time, the Person in Charge had arrived, and directed that the ducks be discarded for safety.

FoodCodeText: Separate types of raw animal foods from other raw animal foods during storage, preparation and display based on cook temperature.
InspectorComments: On the back set of shelves, multiple containers of raw proteins were being stored on lower shelves where raw duck are routinely hung to air dry as a fan blows on them. A large amount of splash was present in a catch pan on the bottom shelf. This can result in cross-contamination between species of protein which have different required cook-temperatures.    Discontinue using this shelf for thawing all frozen foods. Discontinue all hanging of raw, marinated duck on this shelf.     If the duck cannot be prepared by keeping it under refrigeration, remove it from the menu.     Citations will be issued for further observation of this violation.

This is not an effective cooling method, and leaves temperature-abused foods at risk of causing bacterial intoxication.    Discussed the Set & Forget method of cooling, which is validated to always cool foods safely. Work with staff and volunteers to use this method.    1. Let hot foods vent off heat on the countertop for about 20 minutes or until their temperature is approaching about 135F.     2. Spread the food out in shallow containers no deeper than 2 inches    3. FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.

Chef stated the amount of bacon would last them a day or so through the weekend. Leftover product would be placed in the cooler at the end of the shift. Discussed with Chef that the amount of bacon should be portioned into working amounts so that they are used up within 2 hours. Extra product should be pulled if the first portion is used up within 2 hours or less. Bacon was only held out for 1 hour at the time of inspection so the majority was placed into flat containers so that it could cool. Retrain staff to pull small working amounts of product to be used up rapidly so that product is not sitting out at room temperature for extended periods of time. Keep all cold TCS foods at 41F or below.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved chlorine chemical sanitizer solution. The solution must have a minimum concentration of 50 ppm. The solution must also meet the temperature and pH requirements of this rule.

Dish machine data plate requires chlorine as the sanitizer to be used in the machine. Discontinue using dish machine until it is serviced by the provider to change out the lines and replace with chlorine sanitizer. Instructed General Manager to train staff to not mix or interchange chlorine and quat sanitizers. Once machine is serviced, it can be used. Retrain staff on what sanitizers go in the dish machines as required on the intact data plates.

Discussed with Chef that these foods needed to make the 2 hour cooling window from 135F to 70F or below and both were above that first cooling step. Chef opted to discard products. Retrain staff to cool foods from 135F to 70F or below in the first 2 hours, and then from 70F to 41F or below in the remaining 4 hours.

FoodCodeText: Minneapolis food establishments must comply with the food manager certification requirements, as set out in MN Rules, Chapter 4626.2000 to 4626.2525. In support and/or addition to the MN Rules, all persons licensed to operate a food establishment under this chapter (except short-term food establishments) shall at all times employ at least one (1) full time person with supervisory responsibilities (which may be the licensee) who (1) spends a substantial amount of his/her work week at that food establishment, and (2) who has a current Minnesota Department of Health food manager certificate. A large establishment with more than one food preparation and service location under one (1) license, shall have a Minnesota Department of Health certified manager for each location. A new licensee shall provide proof of certification before the facility is approved to open. The licensee shall notify the city when the certified person leaves or terminates employment with the food establishment. A food establishment that no longer employs a certified manager shall employ a certified manager within thirty (30) days. All establishments (except short-term food establishments and those exempted pursuant to rules adopted under the authority of the ordinance) shall maintain up-to-date written policies and guidelines on the premises. These policies and guidelines shall have been approved by the manager of environmental health and shall govern food handling and preparation, sanitation practices and techniques, personal hygiene including handwashing techniques, the prevention of food borne illness through proper receiving, storage, preparation, cooling and reheating of foods, and other related matters. (99-Or-119,§ 1, 10-29-99; 2003-Or-023, ? 2, 2-28-03; 2011-Or-071, ? 6, 8-5-11) Mpls Ord 188.560

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: A Large stainless steel cart of beans approximately 12 inches deep was observed beginning the cooling process and was measured at 68F at the time of inspection. FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.
InspectorComments: Parsley was observed being prepped and chopped with bare hands at the time of inspection. When asked where this parsley was going to be used, Chef stated that it was going to be used as a garnish. Discussed with Chef that foods that are not going through a final cooking step are considered ready-to-eat and are not to be handled with bare hands as this can contaminate the food and spread potential foodborne illnesses. Parsley was repurposed for a stock/soup where it would be cooked thoroughly. Fresh herbs were observed being chopped with bare hands before being placed into a bread crumb mixture. When asked where this bread crumb mixture would be used, it was stated that it would be used as a topping on a finished dish with no further cooking step. Discussed with food employee and Chef that this is another food item that is considered ready-to-eat and its ingredients must not be touched with bare hands. Instructed Chef to pull bread crumb mixture as it could not be served and to make another batch that is not touched with bare hands.  Chives were observed being chopped with bare hands at the time of inspection. When asked where these chives were going to be used, it was found that they were going to be used as a garnish on finished dishes. Discussed with Chef that this is a ready-to-eat food and cannot be touched with bare hands. Instructed Chef to pull chives and either repurpose them into a cooked dish or discard.  Retrain staff to not touch ready-to-eat foods with bare hands and monitor and correct employees who deviate from this safe food practice.   This violation was observed during the previous inspection and during 3 separate occasions during the most recent inspection. As a result, a $200 citation will be assessed to the establishment for this repeat violation.

FoodCodeText: Food employees must wash their hands after: using the toilet; coughing or sneezing; using a handkerchief or disposable tissue; using tobacco; eating or drinking; handling soiled equipment or utensils; caring for or handling service animals or fish in an aquarium, molluscan shellfish or crustacea in a display tank; as frequently as necessary during food preparation to remove soil, contamination, and to prevent cross-contamination when changing food preparation tasks; when switching between working with raw food and working with RTE food; before donning gloves for working with food; and touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean exposed portions of arms.
InspectorComments: A food employee on the cook line was observed moving the garbage bin with gloved hands. They then removed gloves and discarded them and went to retrieve a clean pair of gloves without washing hands. Inspector intervened and required staff member to wash hands before putting on a new pair of gloves. Discussed with manager that when gloves are removed after changing tasks or contaminating gloves, employees must wash their hands before putting on a new pair of gloves to prevent contaminating the new clean gloves. Retrain staff to wash hands after removing gloves and changing tasks. Monitor employees and correct and retrain employees who deviate from this safe food practice.

FoodCodeText: Cool TCS food prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature within 4 hours to 41 degrees F (5 degrees C) or less.
InspectorComments: Banana pancake batter (55F) and Chocolate pancake batter (56F) were observed improperly cooling in deep, lidded containers at the time of inspection after 3.5 hours. Asked the Chef it they would be able to cool the batters down to 41F or lower within the remaining 30 minutes. Chef opted to try to cool the batters in shallow pans no deeper than 2 inches to finish the cooling process. Discussed with Chef that they need to check the temperatures of the batters after 30 minutes and if they were not 41F or below they needed to discard the batter. Retrain staff to change cooling methods to shallow pan cooling and start with cold liquid ingredients to speed cooling. Also discussed uncovering containers for more rapid cooling and monitoring the temperature of the products to ensure that they are indeed cooling to 41F or below in the 4 hours as required. Cool all ambient prepared foods to 41F or below within 4 hours for food safety.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Multiple examples of bulk TCS foods, such as gravy, grits, and cheese sauce, were cooling too slowly, not fully cooling within 6 hours. These foods were observed roughly 5 hours into the cooling curve and were still found between 62 and 68 degrees F. The method was modified to expedite rapid cooling, and effective cooling methods were reviewed. Ensure that all TCS foods are cooling within the above time/temperature parameters.     This issue has been ongoing for the last two inspection cycles. Further non-compliance may result in additional administrative action.

FoodCodeText: Have an item to verify the surface temperature of dishes reaches 160 degrees F inside mechanical hot water dishwashers.
InspectorComments: No test kit on site to measure the plate temperature during a dish cycle. Hot water testing kit options were discussed during the inspection. Provide a means to verify that the plate temperature during a cycle reaches at least 160 degrees F.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Facility is cooling very deeply filled containers of TCS foods some of which solid with an active ice wand and ice bath combo method. Cooling solid foods such as grits at these volumes with an ice wand and ice bath is not an effective cooling method. For solid foods either reduce the volume and stick with the ice method or utilize the 2-inch fill shallow pan method.     All cooling wands inside the cooling foods were melted at the time of the inspection and hadn't been replaced in roughly 3 hours. If continuing to use this ice method replace the ice wand once it melts which will be roughly 1 hour after the cooling process begins.

FoodCodeText: Store food preparation or dispensing utensils that are used with non-TCS foods, such as ice, in a clean, protected location.
InspectorComments: Ice scoops behind the bar were laying within the ice when not in use forcing the bartender to touch the ice with their bare hands to grab the handle. Ice scoops were moved to a metal pan nested inside the ice bin during the inspection. Ensure that ice scoop handles are not laying in the ice in-between uses.

Retrain staff to use rapid cooling methods and to cool foods uncovered, unstacked and spread out.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Observed two pork roasts cooling between 107F-60F on the same roast, they were cooked four hours before temperatures were taken. Ensure cooked time/temperature controlled for safety foods are cooled from 135F-70F within two hours, and from 70-41F within four hours, for a total of six hours to prevent foods from remaining in the temperature danger zone and promoting pathogen growth. the pork roast did not meet the time/temperature requirements and was discarded at time of inspection. Discussed monitoring cooling temperatures and using effective cooling methods with PIC at time of inspection.

FoodCodeText: Have an approved chlorine chemical sanitizer solution. The solution must have a minimum concentration of 50 ppm. The solution must also meet the temperature and pH requirements of this rule.
