Discussed with Chef and Manager that the dish machine should not be used until it can adequately sanitize dishes at 50PPM chlorine. Manager stated they would call a service request in to their service provider to repair the dish machine. Discontinue use until the machine can be repaired and adequately sanitize all dishes at 50PPM chlorine.

FoodCodeText: The consumer advisory disclosure must include either:  • A description of the food as raw or undercooked  • An asterisk to a footnote describing the food as raw or undercooked

Discussed with manager that for each item that customers can request to be served raw or undercooked, there needs to be an asterisk linking the food item to the consumer warning at the bottom of the menu. The consumer warning must be on each page that the menu has raw or undercooked food items on it. Provided consumer advisory guidance document with emailed report for establishment to follow when reprinting their menus. Provide asterisk to consumer advisory on menu to warn customers of the risk of potential foodborne illness when consuming foods that are served raw or undercooked or contain raw or undercooked ingredients.

FoodCodeText: For mechanical dishwashing machines using hot water sanitizing, the surface temperature of the utensils and equipment must reach 160 degrees F or higher.
InspectorComments: High temperature dish machine was not adequately sanitizing dishes to 160F at the time of inspection. Dish machine was run over 5 different cycles and did not sanitize dishes to 160F. Discussed with Person in Charge that dishes must be heated to a minimum of 160F on the rinse cycle to be effectively sanitized. Since the sanitization step was not reached, instructed staff that they could still wash dishes in the dish machine, but they needed to sanitize the dishes using the chemical sanitizer in the 3 basin sink until the dish machine was serviced and sanitizes the dishes at 160F. Ensure the dish machine is reaching 160F to effectively sanitize dishes at all times.

FoodCodeText: Use the approved sanitizer according to the rule and the EPA approved manufacturer's label.
InspectorComments: Sanitizer dispenser at the 3 basin sink was observed measuring 0 oz/gallon concentration at the time of inspection. The sanitizer is a Sink & Surface cleaner sanitizer that requires an effective sanitizing range of 0.27-0.55 oz/gallon. It was found that the liquid in the sink & surface sanitizer container was quat that a staff member had refilled. Discussed with Director that the sanitizer containers should never be poured from one container to another, and that they should never mix sanitizers with each other. Have sanitizer dispenser serviced and use only 1 chemical sanitizer with the dispenser. Retrain staff on handling sanitizer chemicals and ensure they are not mixing or refilling sanitizer containers, and replacing empty containers with the correct sanitizer chemicals. Manually mix sink & surface sanitizer chemical to correct range as required on the label until dispenser is fixed. Use sanitizer according to manufacturer's instructions at all times.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.

A service company had been out to repair the cooler earlier that week but it appeared to have malfunctioned again. There was no food stored in the lower part of the cooler and the upper part of the cooler was temporarily being used to store food during business hours. Discussed with Manager that foods should not be kept in the cooler until it is holding foods at 41F or below at all times. In the meantime, keep Pizza Prep items on a cart and keep in Walk In Cooler. The Pizza Cooler's work surface can be used to prepare the pizzas but the cart must be stored in the Walk In Cooler at all times and only pulled out when it is needed to be used. Once cooler is serviced and holds consistently at 41F or below, use can be restored. All TCS items above held above 41F were discarded by Chef at the time of inspection.

FoodCodeText: Relocate or enclose the utility service lines and pipes so they are not unnecessarily exposed.

At the end of January 2026, there was a water leak from the upper floor of the building that came through the ceiling of the facility in the back hallway by the restrooms and the back kitchen area. Discussed with owner that water baths holding utensils must be kept at 135F or higher to keep utensils properly hot held. Owner removed spatulas and container and placed them in the dish area to be washed. Retrain staff to store utensils in a hot water bath at 135F or higher to safely hot hold used utensils.

Retrain staff to cool in shallow pans to cool foods most rapidly and safely.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.

Discussed with Manager and Chef that foods need to remain uncovered while cooling to cool most rapidly. Cling film was removed from each product to finish their cooling processes. Retrain staff to cool foods uncovered, unstacked and spread out for the fastest and safest cooling processes.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.

Pans were mostly covered with foil, and stacked off-set on top of each other. This was reportedly done due to lack of shelf space for cooling with recent deliveries. Person in Charge brought a rack into the walk-in cooler and placed the pans of egg bake on it individually, with loosened foil to cool.   A container of chicken salad dressing was cooling from recent prep with product about 10 inches deep and covered. Only a one-degree temperature difference was observed across forty minutes. Person in Charge had the dressing divided into two shallow containers and returned to the walk-in uncovered.   Two hotel pans of prepared foods previously cooled were observed with product much closer to 4 inches deep than 2 inches.     Discussed reinforcing with staff that foods must be kept at only two inches deep, and uncovered, for effective cooling. This method has been validated as safe, without needing to monitor times and temperatures of the cooling process. Once foods reach 41F throughout, they can be recombined and/or covered for storage.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Orange Poppy Dressing (56F), Basil Dressing (55F), Caesar Dressing (53F), and Garlic Dressing (57F) were observed being improperly cold held on the counter top of the Salad Prep Cooler at the time of inspection. General Manager stated they had likely been placed out on the countertop at the 11AM opening. Since it was 3.5 hours later when they were measured, manager opted to discard the dressings since it would be difficult to cool them to 41F or below in 30 minutes. Breaded chicken tenders and wings were observed improperly cold holding from 50-53F in the upper part of the Fryer Cooler at the time of inspection and a backup container of breaded chicken was observed at 48F in the lower part of the Fryer Cooler. General Manager turned down the temperature of the unit at the time of inspection and opted to discard the products that were not properly cold held. These items had been placed there the night before and it was not known how long they were cold holding above 41F. Instructed General Manager to discard all TCS products from the cooler and have it serviced before using again.   Mayonnaise was observed improperly cold holding in the Sandwich Cooler at 47F at the time of inspection. It was not known how long it had been holding above 41F. General Manager opted to discard product.  Provided Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) plan with emailed report for dressings that could be held out of temperature control for 4 hours and then discarded as an additional option for compliance. For all other items, maintain all cold TCS foods at 41F or below at all times.

InspectorComments: Sink & Surface Cleaner sanitizer was measured in the 3 basin sink at 0PPM at the time of inspection. Retrain staff to test sanitizer dispenser more frequently and make sure the sanitizer is always used within safe and effective range of 272PPM - 700PPM.

FoodCodeText: A business does not need to submit a HACCP plan for reduced oxygen packaging if foods are:  1. Labeled with date and time they were packaged, and  2. Held at 41 degrees F or less, and  3. Removed from all packaging within 48 hours of sealing.
InspectorComments: Cooked Chicken and Brined olives were observed stored in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) at the time of inspection. Discussed with Chef how long the foods had been in there and it was found that they were prepared on Monday, three days ago. Discussed with Chef that a HACCP plan is needed to use reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) in the establishment for longer than 48 hours. These packages were not labeled with the date and time the products were placed under reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) at the time of inspection.  The only way to ROP without a HACCP plan is to follow 3-502.12F exactly. Chef removed the products from cooler and discarded them. Either discontinue using ROP processes in the facility without a HACCP plan, apply for a ROP HACCP plan before using ROP in the facility, or follow 3-502.12F exactly. If using 3-502.12F, the processes will be evaluated at each inspection to ensure compliance.

Maintain ice machine food contact surfaces clean to sight and touch.

FoodCodeText: Protect food from cross-contamination by using packages or covered containers.
InspectorComments: Containers of raw chicken wings were observed being stacked on top of each other in the lower part of the Prep Cooler with the bottom of the containers touching the food in the containers below it. Discussed with Chef and Manager that containers should have lids or some type of clean barrier when being stacked on top of each other. Discontinue stacking containers in such a manner so that the food is not potentially contaminated.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: A Container of dressed coleslaw in the Prep Cooler was observed cooling at the time of inspection with the cling film tightly covering the food, preventing rapid cooling. Discussed with Chef and Manager that foods that are cooling should remain uncovered until they have cooled to 41F or lower to allow food to cool most rapidly. Retrain staff to cool foods uncovered, unstacked and spread out.

FoodCodeText: All equipment and components must be in good repair. Keep them maintained to manufacturer's specifications.
InspectorComments: The high temperature dish machine's pressure and rinse temperature gauges did not appear to be functioning at the time of inspection. Work with dish machine service provider to repair or replace these dials so they are functioning. Keep all components of the dish machine in good repair at all times.

FoodCodeText: Keep handwashing sinks accessible at all times. Make sure they are only used for handwashing.
InspectorComments: Handwash sink in the bar area was observed with a colander in it. Discussed with lead bartender that the designated handwash sink should be unobstructed and available for handwashing at all times during business hours. Lead bartender removed the colander from the sink immediately. Keep handwashing sink available for handwashing at all times.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Ranch dressing cups were observed cold holding in the upper part of Cooler 2 at 48F at the time of inspection. Dressing cups were stacked above the fill line in the containers. Another container measured at the bottom of the container was measured at 40F. Discussed with Manager and line cook to reduce the fill line of the products so that they are halfway or a single layer of dressings during slow times, and then more can be added to the container in the upper part of the prep cooler once the dressings are used up. Keep backups in the bottom part of the prep cooler or the Reach In Cooler in the back area. Discard all foods that were not held at 41F or below for food safety.

FoodCodeText: Clean surfaces contacting non-TCS foods:  • When surfaces may have been contaminated  • At least once every 24 hours for consumer self-service utensils  • Before restocking consumer self-service equipment and utensils  • As often as needed to keep surfaces clean
InspectorComments: Interior food contact surfaces of 2 of the 3 ice machines were observed with slime mold residue at the time of inspection. Increase cleaning frequency of ice machines and maintain them clean to sight and touch.

FoodCodeText: Thaw TCS food by one of the following methods:  • Inside a refrigerator  • Kept completely under running water of 70 degrees F or less. The food must remain at 41 degrees F or less.  • In a microwave oven  • As part of the cooking process
InspectorComments: Frozen raw beef was observed thawing in the 3 basin sink in sitting water at the time of inspection. Because the outside of the food thaws faster than the inside of the food, the outside of the food can reach above 41F before the inside is thawed completely. Food temperature of outside product was measured at 32F at the time, so instructed Manager to move the item to the Reach In Cooler to finish thawing. Retrain staff to thaw foods under cold running water no warmer than 70F or under refrigeration.

FoodCodeText: Maintain all hot, TCS foods at 135 degrees F or hotter. (Roast beef may be held at 130 degrees F or hotter, if it is cooked according to Part 4626.0340 item B or reheated according to Part 4626.0360, item E.)

Container had been placed there during lunch and was holding at a lower setting than usual. Discussed with Manager that foods need to be hot held at 135F or higher to be safe. Alfredo sauce was placed on a 4 hour discard time from the time it was placed on the Steam Table since it was not known when the sauce had dropped below 135F. Maintain all hot TCS foods at 135F or higher at all times for safety.

Discussed with Chef that equipment needs to fully air dry before being stacked. Retrain staff to allow equipment and containers to fully air dry before stacking or place in storage mode using self-drying positions.

FoodCodeText: Have a ventilation hood system that prevents grease or condensation from collecting on walls or ceilings.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.
InspectorComments: Tuna Salad was observed cooling in the Walk In Cooler with the lid tightly covering the product. This prevents the food from cooling most rapidly and safely. Discussed with Chef that foods need to remain uncovered until they are fully cooled to 41F or lower, then they can be covered. Chef uncovered tuna salad immediately to finish cooling. Gouda hash brown potatoes that had been pre-cooked were observed cooling in the Walk In Cooler stacked perpendicular on top of each other at the time of inspection. This can prevent the food from cooling most rapidly because the pans are stacked so close to each other. Chef rearranged pans so that they were flat on the shelf to cool.  Retrain staff to cool foods uncovered, unstacked and spread out.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed birria meat stored in a large stock pot. Per discussion with the Person In Charge (PIC), the product had been cooling overnight.   Discontinue cooling TCS foods in large, deep containers such as stock pots or deep hotel pans.   These containers prevent rapid heat transfer and keep food in the temperature danger zone, increasing the risk of bacterial growth.   Use approved cooling methods discussed during inspection. More information and guidance have been provided.

FoodCodeText: While TCS foods are cooling, keep containers uncovered, unstacked, and spread out.

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less

Further observation of holding cold TCS foods at improper temperatures will result in citations (fines) and possibly in emergency closure. Emergency closure it an administrative action requiring written plans and procedures to be lifted.      1. The two cold salads for the daily lunchbox area were 75F and 70F. These had been set out for lunch with no temperature control and were discarded. Person in Charge stated they are supposed to be put on an ice bath, but this is not allowed unless they are also managed using Time As A Public Health Control (TPHC). Inspector will provide TPHC template.      2. All foods in the top and bottom of Prep Cooler #3 were above 41F. Raw animal proteins were moved to the walk-in cooler to re-cool. All other TCS foods were discarded to prevent the risk of a foodborne illness called bacterial intoxication.      3. Garlic in oil was observed at 79F on a cart on the cook line. Garlic in oil was discarded after employees first moved it to the cooler. Garlic in oil can cause a deadly form of foodborne illness called Botulism.      4. Cut cabbage was in a tub at 74F. Cut cabbage is a TCS food that can grow bacteria. Cabbage had been cut a couple hours before and was relocated to the walk in cooler.      5. Fried potato fries were observed set out on a shelf above Cooler #4. Fries were discarded.      All TCS foods must be kept at 41F or below - even during busy service periods. (The only exception will be the two salads put in the "lunch box" area, if they are managed using TPHC.)

FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less
InspectorComments: Observed pickled onions made from hot brine in the late morning set into a deep covered 12 Qt cambro container in the walk-in cooler. The product was still at 76F. Based on discussion of when the brine and onions were combined, the product was not discarded but was instead immediately spread out for more effective cooling intended to force the product below 70F within two hours of when it was estimated to have reached 135F. Without this immediate intervention, the safe cooling times and temperatures listed above would not have been met.       Train employees to use the 2-inch fill method described below in 3-501.15A to effectively achieve safe cooling times and temperatures.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed pickled onions made from hot brine in the late morning set into a deep covered 12 Qt cambro container in the walk-in cooler. This is not an effective method for cooling TCS foods.   Person in Charge immediately divided the onions into two portions in hotel pans, with the onions no deeper than 2 inches in each pan. Pans were set back into the walk-in cooler, uncovered to cool.      Train employees to use the 2-inch fill method to effectively cool prepared TCS foods. This is the only method validated to work without a large amount of ice and dedicated staff intervention:  Put hot food in pans with the food no deeper (or thicker) than 2 inches, set them uncovered in the walk-in cooler and leave them there. After the food has reached 41F or less throughout, the food can be combined and/or covered for storage.

FoodCodeText: Use effective cooling methods to cool TCS foods.
InspectorComments: Observed cooked, ground beef set in a deep quarter hotel pan covered with aluminum foil, to "cool" from earlier being cooked on the truck. FoodCodeText: Cool cooked TCS food:  • Within two hours from 135 to 70 degrees F, and  • Within a total of six hours from 135 to 41 degrees F or less

The risk of causing foodborne illness by bacterial intoxication in this scenario is high.       FOOD TRUCKS ARE NOT ALLOWED TO COOL PREPARED TCS FOODS ON THE VEHICLE.   See report comments for corrective actions allowed at time of this inspection.

FoodCodeText: Sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils after cleaning by using an approved chemical sanitizer in manual or mechanical operations for at least 7 or 10 seconds for chlorine depending on temperature, concentration, and pH; and 30 seconds for all other chemical sanitizers or an contact time used in relation with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH.
InspectorComments: Bar dishwasher was run over several cycles and did not reach the minimum required 50PPM chlorine sanitizer concentration to adequately sanitize bar glassware at the time of inspection. Worked with Manager to troubleshoot dishwasher and replaced the container of sanitizer with a new container to see if that corrected the issue. After several cycles and priming the sanitizer line, dish machine was measured again at 100PPM chlorine. Discussed with Manager that dishwasher should be tested before dishes are washed in the machine so that they are adequately sanitized; if dish machine is not sanitizing, it needs to be brought to the attention of the Person In Charge to address. Maintain chlorine sanitizer at 50PPM minimum to safely and effectively sanitize dishes.

FoodCodeText: In addition to floor requirements found in the Minnesota Food Code, floors in all rooms in which food or drink is stored or prepared, in which multiuse utensils are washed, and in walk-in refrigerators, dressing or locker rooms and toilet rooms shall be a smooth, durable, easily cleanable, non absorbent, light-colored material. Permissible materials include, but are not limited to, terrazzo, ceramic tile, quarry tile, or plastic or plastic coating over tight wood or concrete floors or equivalent. The floor covering must be grease resistant in all areas where grease or fatty substances are normally used and may drip or spill on the floor. In every new or remodeled food establishment a coved juncture of at least one-quarter-inch radius between the floor and the wall, except in serving areas, shall be constructed or installed. All exterior areas where food is served shall be kept properly drained. (99-Or-119,§ 1, 10-29-99)

FoodCodeText: The business needs to submit a HACCP plan to reduce oxygen package:  • Raw meats  • Raw vegetables  • USDA or equal to cured meats received in an intact package
InspectorComments: Guacamole was observed stored in vaccuum sealed bags for over 48 hours without a HACCP plan. Discussed with Chef and General Manager that foods can only be vacuum sealed under a 48 hour exemption and must be labeled with date and time on each individual package. Discontinue using extended vacuum sealing method without a HACCP plan or use proper 48 hour procedure. Discard packages of vacuum sealed foods that are not labeled and extend beyond 48 hours under vacuum seal until a HACCP plan has been completed and approved. Provided HACCP resources to operator with emailed report.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: Roasted garlic oil was observed being cold held on the top of the Expo Cooler at 69F at the time of inspection. Discussed with Chef and General Manager that roasted garlic oil, even strained, needs to be kept cold at 41F or lower, or hot held at 135F or higher to keep it from growing harmful bacteria that can make people sick. Discard garlic oil since it has been out of temperature control for longer than 4 hours and store garlic oil under temperature control at 41F or lower to keep it safe for consumption.

FoodCodeText: Keep all cold TCS foods at 41 degrees F or colder under mechanical refrigeration.
InspectorComments: House made Garlic Butter (69F) was observed improperly cold held on the top of the Prep Cooler at the time of inspection. Person in Charge stated that they take the butter out to soften at open in the morning and keep it out until the end of the day, then it is placed back into the cooler. This is not an approved practice, since garlic butter is a TCS food that requires refrigeration at all times and can grow bacteria that makes people sick if not properly refrigerated. Discussed several options for allowing the garlic butter to soften while ensuring safe food handling, such as using Time as a Public Health Control (TPHC) or lab analysis options to prove the item is shelf stable. Provided these resources with emailed report. Maintain all cold TCS foods at 41F or lower at all times.

FoodCodeText: Thaw TCS food by one of the following methods:  • Inside a refrigerator  • Kept completely under running water of 70 degrees F or less. The food must remain at 41 degrees F or less.  • In a microwave oven  • As part of the cooking process
InspectorComments: Garlic Butter containers that were previously frozen were observed being thawed out at room temperature in the food preparation sink at the time of inspection. Discussed with staff that foods that are required to be refrigerated must be thawed under refrigeration so that all parts of the foods are 41F at all times during the thawing process. Items were still frozen so they were placed back into the cooler to finish thawing under refrigeration. Thaw frozen TCS foods under refrigeration so that all parts are cold 41F or lower at all times.

FoodCodeText: Mount the spray arm so it cannot hang below the spill rim of a sink or provide an approved backflow prevention device on the faucet.
InspectorComments: The spray arm installed on the wash compartment faucet of the 3 basin sink was observed hanging well below the flood rim of the sink at the time of inspection. The hose and faucet do not have an apparent backflow prevention device that prevents grey water from being sucked back up into the fresh water supply, and this creates a contamination issue. Discussed with staff that the spray arm needs to be mounted above the flood rim to provide an air gap since the faucet does not have an air gap. Provide this air gap to protect the water supply.

FoodCodeText: Make sure all ready-to-eat foods and garnishes are not touched with bare hands.

Wrap was discarded and a new wrap was made after staff member washed hands and put on a pair of gloves. Do not prepare ready-to-eat foods with bare hands.

FoodCodeText: Use a consumer advisory to inform customers of the increased risk of consuming raw or undercooked animal foods.
